title: D'Andre Swift, Luther Burden III, Grady Jarrett talk offseason work | Press Conference
text: back to your production from last season. Your reflection, what were the things that stood out to you what last season was for you? >> Uh, me personally, thought it was a good year. Um, solid. Um, was able to capitalize off the opportunities I was given. Um, I still feel like I left some out there. Um, that's me just being critical on myself. Um, looking back over everything, for the most part, I think I did a good job of doing what I was asked to do. >> You sense you left out there. What were some of the things that >> little stuff, detailed stuff as far as tracks, aiming points, just being consistent with those type of things, just not really veering off too much from that? Yeah, from that standpoint. >> You feel highly about what your relationship was with Coach D? >> Yeah, he's going to miss most about him being gone and then what's the process like to coach? >> Oh man, he uh he was great for us. Not as uh just running back group, but offensively and the team wise, just the energy part every single day. um somebody that's at least his print um if he was here when he was here. So um can't replace nobody like that. Um excited for him as new opportunity though. >> Is there anything you like about Eric being gone? Anything you don't have to hear anymore? >> Looking for something, huh? Uh >> no, he was good, man. He was good. Um I try to navigate to any coaching style that I'm given to. Um nothing bad to say about that man at all. >> What have you noticed about uh Steuville so far? He's been great so far. Um, great deal of respect for him. He's been doing this for a high a high at a high level for a long time. Um, he's a great teacher. I I could tell that already. Um, he's great for us. He's real relatable. Um, he's been great for us so far. >> Talked about things moving a little faster for the guys that were here last year coming back for year two. What have you seen from the guys that are now in the second year in this offense? >> Just them um trying to take that next step as far as nothing's too differently too different offensively. So, us kind of hitting the grass and kind of like taking it up a notch like it's time to go. We can't really We ain't looking forward to going back. We're looking to go back at all. We need to >> set the standard and continue that standard that we that we kind of built off last year and then um just kind of take it up a notch for sure. You >> guys had a couple pre- snap penalties today concern you and where we are. >> Uh it's early. It's early. Um day two out there, second install. Um, and that's us trying to be perfect and I think um, move too fast um, as far as us players trying to be perfect, be at the right spot and things like that. But takes time, I guess, for sure. >> What's What's it mean for you to have same playbook, same quarterback, four of the five offensive linemen back as you get into this season? >> I'm happy. I'm excited. I'm excited for this year. I'm excited to be uh these guys and be able to continue to build >> the uh the wheel route where Caleb found you on it down the right sideline. Did you know you're getting the ball in that play? >> Um once I took off and I seen um how it was played, I was hoping so. When I looked up and the ball was there, great ball, great placement, I was able to make a play for him. Yeah. >> Do you sense any more confidence in Caleb or just more comfort comfortability what he's doing this time of year? definitely a little bit more comfortable um second year with him being with Ben and in the same system. That's with anybody that's in the same system, you should be more comfortable the second time around. Um but I could I could just see uh his urge to get back to it. >> And same similar, but Luther Burton uh Ben was saying earlier he's like I'm buying stock and him noticed the last couple days. >> You see the same do you see the same thing as a guy who's kind of used to what and how to do things around here? got a young man that's that's hungry, that knows uh his ability, confident, goes out there every day, goes to work, and he like he knows his ability. So, and it shows. >> Andrew, how do you how do you sense his hunger? >> I sensed it last year when he first walked in the building, once you meet him and talk to him and see his style of play, like what you see is what you get. That's how who he is every single day. And you're a dog. >> The the year the players get drafted, you know, they always talk about having a short off seasonason, you know, they got to prepare for the combine. >> Yeah. and kind of, you know, learn a new place, learn a new playbook. For a second year player like Burton, what's just the benefit of having a full off seasonason and being able to, you know, act kind of more like a veteran would? >> Um, and being able to come back to the same spot to where as though the coaches are the same, the playbook is the same, the quarterback is the same. Um, that means a lot. Um, don't have really have to learn everything all over again. just um look at back on your first year and see what you need to correct and work on them things day in and day out. Yeah. >> The year the years where you've had bigger production receiving wise, what worked well for you in those situations? >> Um the quarterback finding me, being being able to make make things happen. That's it. Just really just getting the ball in my hands. That's it. >> What do you think the the strongest part of the combination of you and Kyle is? There's no drop off um at all. Uh he's able to do everything. I'm able to do everything. Um it's tough on defense is when I make something happen, his number gets called, he's make something happen. Like what you going to do? You know what I mean? Especially with the O line we have and how them guys are coached and um the way Ben's system is like it's it's a lot for a defense to account for for four quarters. >> With the offensive line, you'll have a new center, new left tackle. What's the challenge for the facts of just getting uh the chemistry, I guess, with the guys in front of you? >> I mean, all that stuff take time. Um, and it's hard to do that without pads on and stuff like that, but um just uh creating a relationship with them new guys and um just continue every time we walk in this building, keep building and um just uh just going to work together, man. And that's that's it's going to speak volumes when we get on this run, we get season starts and things like that. Yeah. >> How would you and Kyle benefit from working with each other? Obviously, he comes in as a group. I don't know how hesitant he was to ask you questions, but do you even learn some things from him like he was? How do you guys help each other on and off? >> Uh, we always talk talk. Um, anything he sees or I see, we always go to each other. Um, I asked in the day out there on a little route I had like, did you see that? Was it something inside of me? Was it something outside of me? Like, just talk ball. Just talk ball. And it's um, and it's vice versa. >> It'll probably be better than actually this summer. But did you notice anything from Deon Bush out there at linebacker his style of play? speed. >> Yeah, I've been a big fan big fan of him um when he was in college. Um his play speed, jumps off jumps off the film. Um he's been doing it for a long time at a high level as well. Um >> yeah, he's going to be a great addition for us. >> With uh with how much with how much you guys were able to turn it last year, get get in the playoffs, win a game, do you and now coming back here with the same coaches, do you allow yourself to dream it sort of in a different way of like what could be possible this year? >> Uh we start all over. I we ain't thinking about last year. Um, new opportunity. That's how I look at it. Um, what we did last year was last year. Like, uh, a whole new season, whole new opportunity, man. Um, one that I'm excited for just just to build off of it. It was a good last year. I'm not going to downplay it at all, but um, it's over with. We got to do more. >> How much pride do you take that you and Kyle back? Is that something you guys talked about? Is that something like after the season? uh really talk about it too much. Um once like people bring it to our attention, it's something cool to sit down and look at. But like when we miss the season, we not really think about that stuff too much, but it's cool. It's cool to see once you see the statistics and things like that when they do come out at the end of the season what we were able to do. Um I think can only be better. >> Feeling the conversation that you are this big breakout. Do you feel like that? I mean, I know you do, but you kind of felt like that when you first walked in here last year. But do you feel like you're about to introduce yourself to the real in a whole new way? >> Uh, I feel like only the real know, man. You know, you know. So, um, I'm just locked in every single day, you know, coming here ready to work, you know, ready to get better, ready to get coached up, and, you know, ready to win games. How different is it for you to have the off seasonason where you know the coach, you know the playbook, you know the quarterback, you know what's expected of you as opposed to last year where everything was really new with this time of year and you were a little banged up too. >> Um it's definitely, you know, a blessing, you know, um to have the same coaches, you know, come back, you know, same group of guys for the most part. Um and to be familiar with, you know, the scheme, the system, and um you know, who I'm working with, you know, earning those guys trust still every day. So, um, no, we're just working. >> Stood out there this morning and said he finds stock in you. What do you think you've done to get his his attention in that way? >> Nothing. What do you What do you think he sees in you? >> Uh, sure. You got to ask him, man. Um, I just come to work every day and do my job, you know, the best of my ability and um, you know, I leave the rest to everybody else. >> I don't think we've talked to you since DJ uh, left. are your responsibility any extra added responsibility now that that room is missing a veteran and and the team's missing somebody who was a playmaker. >> Uh I just feel like you know somebody else in the room got to step up. Um so um you know you got to step up when know when your number call. Um DJ was a great player for us. Um a great leader for us great leader for the room. Um sure somebody got step up. >> What does stepping up look like to you? >> Um making plays you know knowing what you're supposed to do. knowing how you supposed to do it the right way. Um, detailed it up. Um, shoot. That's that's pretty much what you do this off season to have yourself be more ready to take that next step forward. >> Um, I was here >> I was just here working working. >> What were some of the focal points for you of your offseason? >> Um, I was just trying to get bigger, bigger, faster, stronger. Um, you know, get more familiar with the playbook. Make sure you know um I come in comfortable, you know, so um I can play faster. Where do you see yourself in that regard in terms of the the comfort in the system kind of reducing the hesitation that might have existed as a rookie? >> Um I feel like it's going to be good, you know, just so um I'll be able to play way faster. So um less thinking, more plan, more explosive plays, more excitement. So um that's what I'm bringing. >> Randall said last week that he's seen a dramatic improvement in just alignment and assignment stuff from you. What's your self assessment of of what's produced that growth for you? Um, you know, just studying my playbook, you know, um, continue to have, you know, conversations with the quarterback. Um, how he see things, how I see things, how we can, you know, just get better. Um, so we just here working and trying to get better each and every day. >> What's that process look like with, uh, getting on the same page with Caleb? Like what are the discussions? >> Um, so I guess like if we miss a, you know, ball, we'll, um, talk about to, see what we had did better. Um, so stuff like that. And, um, you know, just trying to connect. You went out to USC with him, right? >> One play today where I saw you and a conversation about it. Do you remember that or like what what was being discussed at that point? It's kind of a high. >> No, I don't remember. >> You went to Caleb. you went to USC with so what's the value of that for you um just not only in team building but in in being able to work with the quarterback uh in the offseason I >> it's great um I mean because we offer um a certain amount of time and um you know you want to get back you know on the same page as the quarterback um and you know get that chemistry back up and where it was where it was you know from the end of the season so we're just looking to continue to make that grow >> DeAndre S just in you're talking about you're you're a hungry guy you were a hungry guy going last year. You're still a hungry guy. What are you hungry to do? >> Um, just prove, you know, >> that I am who I say I am. >> And what is that >> guy? Something last year that because of injury, because of, you know, the amount of guys you had in the receiver room that you feel this year you're going to have a better opportunity to put on display? >> Um, I feel like, man, you just go out there, you make plays, you know, coach B going to want to give you the ball more. So you go out there, make a play, coach being gonna get you right. >> A lot of times when people come to Chicago, it take them a while to get acclimated to what the Bears Packers thing is. You and Coach Johnson came in and leaned all the way into it. You got the iconic photo, you got the quotes about Green Bay Packing. Now that you've leaned into it so much, what does it mean to you now? And are you looking forward to those games? And do you feel like it's going to be a target on you from that second day? >> Uh, no. I'm just looking for week one. whoever on the week that week, that's what I'm looking for. So, >> what have you seen from Zavon Thomas so far? >> Uh, I see he he's a electric player. Um, he had a great fade ball today. Um, thought going to be a great player for us and made big plays for us this year and um, it's going to be exciting to watch. >> What can you carry over from having DJ in the room last year? Like, what will be some of the things he's left with >> Um, just how to be a pro. Um, I mean, he was probably the first guy in here every morning I came in and that was about 6:30, 7:00 a.m. So, um, just seeing how he take care of his body, how he, you know, prepares himself for practice, games, stuff like that, and, you know, just picking his brain. Um, it was great. And, um, >> what was your reaction when they traded him? >> Um, I was sad, of course. Um, I mean, um, you know, he was a great teammate. He was, um, a great leader for, you know, the whole group, the whole team. And um I'm excited he's um in a great situation. Um and >> Ben also said this morning that you're playing faster. Do you feel that way? Do you feel like you're playing faster? >> Oh, yeah. Yeah, I'm playing way faster. Um less thinking, just going out there trying to make plays. >> What What does playing faster out there mean to you and how does it translate, you think, on the field? >> Uh I feel like it helps way better. I mean, it helps a lot because um if you thinking what you got to do, you can't even like focus on what the defense is in. You trying to focus on what you got to do. So, if you already know what you got to do, um I feel like you have a better plan of how to attack the defense. >> What What's the best part of playing for Ben? >> Winning better best, baby. >> Play deep ball to to Rome today. That big completion. Did you have a good view on that? >> Oh, yeah. Yeah. Y'all saw me. >> I already knew it was money. I just looked back. Yeah, it was a uh it was a great play. Him and Rome got a great connection. Um we've been working on our scrimmer drill a lot this year. Um you know, the coaches harping on it. Um so um it was great to see it happen in practice. Um so let's continue to do that. >> By the time you finally got going off your injury and kind of getting more opportunities in the offense, Ron was kind of coming down. He had got his injury. His production kind of slipped off. What's the chemistry? What's the process of getting y'all two on the same page as being the one two punch trying to make? >> Um, I mean, I don't know. I don't lie. Shoot. Just, you know, trying to stay healthy as much as possible, stay on the field, um, learn from each other. That's a great way to, you know, pick each other brain and, um, you just have that connection. >> What is it like to work with a quarterback who can make throws like Caleb can? What's it like to be know you're on the other end of that? >> Um, it's amazing to watch. just amazing to be a part of. Um it's just very like real special like very quarterbacks can do what he do. So um exciting to watch him man. >> How do you uh cut down on the or help cut down on the pre- snap uh penalties like not have a repeat of what you guys went through? >> You said how can we >> Yeah. like uh how can you as a group get together and not have a repeat of the pre- snap penalties uh issue? You had a couple of uh as an offense today. >> Um I feel like we just got to have, you know, clean operation. Um we just got to have clean operation. Everybody got to, you know, pick their stuff up and um got to stay focused. >> I saw that you had started a YouTube channel, started posting more. Did you feel like because you were more comfortable here that you were able to kind of focus on some other things, not just zero in on everything is football 24/7? >> No, I had a YouTube before I got to the league. So, YouTube just something I do. >> You doing? >> Yeah. >> Did the cooking show reach out to you or did you seek them out? >> They reached out to me. >> All good. Thank you. >> Both DA and and coach Garrett were talking about focusing on technique and fundamentals on the runway to OTAAS. What did you experience in terms of defensive line really zeroing in on that the last few? >> Yeah, you can feel it from day one day one of u this program we started. We we really really took it to the basics and I um I think it's been super helpful. It's helping helping us. we can see the um the progress of it on the field already with just two practices and just the way we speak to each other um speak through what's expected um the details of whether it's stance or finishing at the ball how we need to we breaking it down and um we we we definitely letting the standard know be early what's expected >> on the finish front. What is some of the things that that come down to the details and the basics of finishing? Well, to get to the finish, that's a good question, but we got to have a good start. And that's one of the biggest things we've been focusing on is the start, whether it's our stance, um, knowing the mindset and how we're going to play a certain play, technique, and um, so to get to the basis of our better finish that we need and what everybody is accounting for and looking for, we go back to our basics and getting our start right and then what's expected from us from a mindset standpoint and physically to get the job done. What's the what's the best part about coming off of a good season in terms of confidence and and everything? And what's the what's the biggest trap? >> I think the best part is uh seeing the rewards of hard work. Uh some dedication, overcoming hardships and uh believing in each other and the teammates. That's definitely a good thing. um as far as maintaining that and things that can be traps or thinking that you can just show up again and it's just going to happen and you can do the same things without putting in the same kind of required work or thinking it's going to take you going to do the same thing you did to achieve the same outcome but sometime it take more or whether more it might be a different strategy and um knowing how team's going to you know prepare for you now they got another year tape on you doing certain things so having the ability to adjust I think is paramount but also having the mindset to really just um go back to the drawing board, go back to the take take it back to the basics and uh that's the hard part, man. Just the consistency, excuse me, the consistency and um just always just, you know, stacking days on top of days, going back through all over again and not knowing that you just never arrived. >> There weren't a lot of personnel changes on the defensive line. Do you think more production up front is just a matter of health and you guys staying healthy? >> I I do think that's a big part of us staying healthy. we we we all were kind of bit some ways somehow by the injury bug last year. Um but that all goes into you know the preparation and just how we take care of oursel and how we go through our processes and stuff like that. But I definitely think um health is up there but also like we talked about earlier um doing a lot of self scout seeing where we can get better at and also you know the coaches believing in us the guys that's in the room knowing if we just focus more on on these things that we can get the job accomplished. So it's up to us as players to go out here and get it done. Um because obviously the coaches and personnel department believe in us to do a job at a high level and that's what we need to go do. >> How much do you guys in that room hear all that outside talk that they're they need to add somebody to that defensive line to >> Yeah. Yeah. We all got cell phones and internet so no. So we hear it man. But it also it come with the job you know. It come with a job and um at the end of the day so you know but we got to be we got to really take it personal and and and be get back to work you know. and day even if sometimes your best ain't good enough you know so you got to find out where can I be better at where can I you know so it all go together but um all we can do as a as a unit is look in the mirror and challenge oursel every day to go be better and um do what we need to do to have um better you know better output >> you kind of just hit on it with question but how much did your knee hamper you last year and then what goes into the maintenance to kind of be more proactive in dealing with it >> yeah so I mean um I got hurt pretty early in the season. Um try to get through it and then obviously had to you know make some adjustments and be able to come back and just really be you know um wound it back up into the lineup and towards the end start playing a lot better as I felt better. But um I mean I just you know sometimes things happen you know sometimes things happen and there really not a reason for it. For me it was kind of like a divine intervention to be honest. U it gave me a lot of chance to kind of self-reflect. A lot of stuff moved fast in my life as far as when getting me here doing things. So, I was really just on just as you can know, you guys talk to me a lot and just passion and fired up and just things like I was I was like that all the time. You know what I'm saying? And um it really gave me a chance to really just really just take a breath, see where I'm at. And um by the time I came back, I was able to help contribute to the team and get us where we were. But um I mean, I just got to be smart, listen to my body more, and um it ain't a lack it ain't a lack of putting in work. I could tell you that. So maybe it's want pulling back here doing this or you know just doing some things different. You know obviously I'm 33 year old now and which is a honor. A lot of people look at as a bad thing. So you going to find out you were 33 built like this right here. So I take a lot of pride in it and um it's it's exciting to be feeling a lot better this year and I know that I owe Chicago a better year and I'm excited to go go do that. where you went with that the the the December and January tape you put out. What did you see on there that would that that satisfied you, I guess, in regards to >> um obviously just I mean really just just just running without limp, you know what I'm saying? Like feeling better and and and obviously just being able to play with more confidence and uh let letting the body heal up more, but also just knowing we was in that crunch time, too. and whether it was the pain I was going through, whatever I had to do daily throughout the week, it really didn't matter because we trying to make this playoff Super Bowl push, you know. So, that's kind of where I was at and um really just really just took it there and just let let everything, you know, I wasn't really worried about whether I was getting going to get hurt again or do this and do that. I was just trying to put my best foot forward every day whenever my number was called and just show up and um so I'm excited to put a full season together and and do what I need to do. >> What were you like when you had to slow down? Was that that were did you enjoy it in the time? Did it drive you crazy? >> Um, not I mean not necessarily because you got to do what you got to do to get your body right, you know. And um and uh it's just adjustment. I don't know if slow down is the right word. It's just maybe just adjustments here and there. And that's one thing I do appreciate about the staff so much is um and when I say staff, I'm talking about strength coaches and and coaches cuz we we talk through these things and we develop plans and you know how we can adjust better cuz obviously it was my first first year first season last year. So, we hadn't spent a lot of time together, you know, and um so at this point now coming in early before the offseason program start and um spending time with them working every day, going out here working every day, we able to develop a plan and how we want to move forward going through the season. And uh so that's why I think it's so critical, especially for me at this point in my career, to spend the time and be here um so we can have the best season we can have. >> Been doing this at a high level for a long time. when you hear get back to the fundamentals, get back to the technique. Were there things that were pointed out in your game last year outside of just being injured that you like, man, I didn't even notice I've been doing that for this long? >> Yes, sir. >> I fix that. I'm getting to the quarterback. >> A lot. A lot. And and that's what I was talking about um earlier about fixing the start and um really being self-critical. And that's one thing I could definitely appreciate about um just being here is because it's going to make me a better player. It's gonna make us all a better player. and um and when you you can push in on tape and see what the difference is and what the difference can be if we tweak this and tweak that, you got no choice but to buy in. So there's a lot in the game that's within my control that can make me a much better player even at this point in my career. So I can appreciate that for sure. >> Part of that that's hard where you like I've been doing this for this long. I know it works. >> I mean that guys like that they don't they don't they don't make it to year 12. They don't make it to their cuz because you got to you you never make it. You know what I'm saying? like you always got to be coachable. You always got to be able to make adjustments because um I don't I don't I just think whenever you see people who the best at what they do, they always trying to get better, man. That's why you see guys like, you know, LeBron James playing 23 years, working out year round, you know, Derek J play for however long he did, always looking at the small things. I'm just thinking about some of the great Tiger Woods, like when he was the best at that, he just talked about the start, talking about his working fundamentals all the time. So, how can I I mean, I've did some nice things in my career, but I ain't did no Michael Jordan, no LeBron James stuff so far, but how can they say I'mma put in my work every day, and I think I'll arrive, you know? So, just humbling yourself and also thinking like, you know, why not try to be the best you can be every day? >> U you got a lot of new personalities in the room. What have you learned about like Neville Gam Galammore and Contavis Street or the rookie Jordan Van? >> Yeah, well, um I played with Contavis three years in Atlanta. uh he's going to bring a lot to the room. Uh Neville Gallammore is a guy who's strong, fast. Um I think he fit the bill of what we want to accomplish here. So I think it's um and then also having Lynch here from Tennessee. I think he played a lot of good football. So we got a really good room and obviously me and Dexter coming back from last year. I think we got a really good room combination of guys and these young rookies we have worked really hard too and they put in a lot of good work. So I'm excited for our interior group to see what we really can do. And um as long as we do what they asking us to do, I think we'll cause a lot of havoc. There was there was so much talk last year about the gratitude of the the locker room vibes and how that was such a an engine for you guys of having that. How do you recreate that in a different version with a new group? >> I mean got to get to know your teammates more, you know, and then like I say, just putting in the work. Nothing better than just putting in the work with each other. That's how you really grow the bond, you know, gain the mutual respect for each other and seeing seeing how each other grind and go do what we need to do. And uh so it's just like everything, it's new year obviously in the NFL. Every year is a new locker room and we just got to make this one the best we can and let the relationships become organic and do what they do. >> Obviously new voices behind linebacker safety. What's the adjustment period? Getting used to who voices the call everybody. >> It's still early, you know, it's still early and obviously going to be an adjustment. Um but the scheme of the defense is when everybody you got a good understanding of what's expected. Um, I think it helps. Um, so, so like I say, we we we we real early obviously as we just had our second practice and it's going to get better and better. So, um, so and obviously the guys will be here if they can get a job done. So, >> I'm sure you get asked this every May, but why is it important for you to be here at this point in your career? >> Um, I think just spending the time in the building like I said earlier, I think it's just one enjoying what you do for work. You know, I enjoy working out. I enjoy football. Um, not really much else I want to be doing right now, you know. Uh, so, uh, I I like being here. I like being around the game. Um, and, uh, I mean, just really trying to find the things in my game to where I can continue to be better and to spend this time with each other as a team. I think it's critical, you know, that our our our season is made in the offseason, I think. And that and I truly believe that. And, um, I've learned that, too, because I it has been pieces in my career where I wasn't at OTAAS all the time and I'll show up when it's just time to practice. And I've seen now as I've become more mature where that may have been a shortcoming for me, especially being a leader. I've always been a leader in the cap, you know what I'm saying? So being around helps, you know, and and it matters. So um just learning from mistakes in my past and also um appreciating where I am right now and just taking it day by day, being able to put in good work. >> Obviously you spent a lot of time in Atlanta. What do you think when you heard that Jordan Vandenberg started a laundromat business in there? >> Uh I just learned that. I just I did not know that. I didn't know that. But I mean, there's a lot of opportunity in Atlanta. It's a beautiful city and I think he, you know, he went Georgia Tech, so I guess hope it work out for him. >> Can you have a can you have a regular offseason right now, Grady? Like, are you pass everything from last year as far as working out or you have to, you're still kind of getting like peak form, I guess. >> Oh, no. I've been working out. Yeah, I've been doing everything and um having all my reps practice, doing all my running, conditioning as far as my health is what you're asking or >> Yeah. Yeah. >> Yeah. Yeah. Good. Congrats to him, man. I don't think we need him to do our laundry, though.

title: Ben Johnson on start of OTAs | Press Conference
text: All right, here we go. Uh, good to see everybody today. Um, I just share with what we talked about with the players yesterday is is building our foundation and uh, you know, I think we're off to a really good start and has a lot to do with how we go about our business, particularly now that we're on the grass together as a as a full 90man roster, uh, coaches and players together on this thing. and uh you know what we want our body language to be like, what we want our finish to be like, the communication, our daily habits, the discipline, the consistency with which we want to approach each and every day. And so yesterday was a great start for us. Um here's what I know about our group right now. We got a bunch of really hard workers. I couldn't be more impressed with the last five weeks, five and a half weeks now, and how they've approached their business. So, um really excited here to to uh get another good day of OTAAS in open it up from there. Ben, what feels sharper to you or more in place to you as the head coach than last year when you were going when you were in this part of the calendar? >> Well, yeah. I mean, uh it's it's everything. It's it's uh the entire team just everyone knows what the expectations are in the building. Um what meetings look like. Uh we talked about that meetings, walk through practice. Um, you know, it's noticeable to me just one day of OTAAS, the guys that were here last year versus the new guys to the program, whether they're rookies or free agents, there's just a a different level of I don't want to say comfort, but they they know they know what it's supposed to look like. And so, um, that's a good thing. That's a good thing. We can kind of hit the ground running a little bit from an offensive perspective. You certainly see, um, a lot of guys picking up where where they left off. And uh I know our our quarterback rooms at a different place than it was a year ago. Our route runners certainly feel that way from how we do routes on air to what it looks like in a team setting. Um O line, you know, those coaches do a phenomenal job with those guys. And um same thing there. You see that guys aren't thinking quite as much. They're now being able to play faster. Um defensively, you see the same thing going on. I feel strongly about how we're coaching them. We went back to the fundamentals on all three levels of our defense and uh and that showed up yesterday. So, we're off to a good start. We'll we'll see what the the rest of the way looks like. >> Specifically with Caleb on that piece, what are you able to cut through with him now that you weren't able to? I know it's not fundamental. You're not going to skip those things. Maybe communication or what type of things can you kind of cut through with him now that you weren't able to last year? >> Well, I mean, we we were I think you guys saw it. We struggled to break the huddle at times last year in the spring and in training camp. And uh you know, like I said, one day down, but we didn't have that issue. So, the the communication in the huddle, what it looks like to break the huddle, the urgency to the line of scrimmage, the tempo that we want to stress the defense with. Um the quarterback plays a huge part in that. He orchestrates the whole operation, and those guys have taken that to heart. And uh and so from that aspect, um feel really good about where we're at. Now it's the next level of each each concept. What are we trying to do? And um potentially expanding on, hey, here's your progression 1, two, three to how can we accelerate our eyes, our vision, what are we looking for um some coverage indicators to where we might take more alerts, um things of that nature. So a little bit more minut, uh those guys have been really receptive to it. >> Married up with that with the minutiae in the name of making Caleb more efficient as a quarterback. How do you go about sort of programming the efficiency without turning him into a robot and and making sure that he still uses his artistry, I guess. >> Well, I think you get what you emphasize. That's that's what I've learned in this industry and um you know, ball security takeaway something we emphasize. We'll continue to emphasize it. That shows up. Uh completion percentage is something that we're we're going to emphasize. And so what did they get when they came into the offensive meeting today? They got the the chart of what was our completion percentage yesterday. um who had drops, what did our scramble drill look like when when those naturally occurred. Um and so that that's really our our first objective is just drawing more attention to it. Those guys are really critical of themselves in drill settings, uh routes on air, where the ball placement is. We we want to give these these pass catchers, we have so many talented ones, opportunities to run after the catch. And so, um we're being very critical on on where we're putting that football with them. And and that's something that we grade every day. Luther Burton didn't have much of an off season last year. You know, he went through the draft process, then he gets hurt. What's the value of having him healthy and and good for this time of year? >> Yeah, I'm buying Luther Burden stock right now. Just how he's approached his off season. It's been uh it's been electric. That showed up yesterday. He had numerous explosive plays. I loved how in phase two he was finishing every single rep that he took. Uh and that really translated over to yesterday as well. So, he's in a really good spot. He's still developing and growing his route tree. Coach L and and Isaiah Ford, they've done a phenomenal job with him just working to develop those things. Speed cuts to sharp breaks, releases, things of that nature. And um he's been extremely coachable. So I I'm I'm really happy with him. >> Is this your vision obviously when you drafted him or has he shown you things that surprised? >> Well, I think when when we drafted him, we saw an explosive athlete who was really dangerous with the ball in his hands. The question was how can we get it in his hands? Um the easy things to do are screens or or short throws, but I think there's a lot more to his game that um we've worked to unlock and he's been really receptive to to how we can get that done. He ran a route yesterday that was the first time he'd ran that route and he he ran as well as I've been around. So um thing things like that really get you excited as a coach. >> Have you seen his route running grow from the day he walked in here last year to when you saw him? >> Yeah. Well, he he looks like he's playing at a different speed right now and you knew he had it in him. He's a 4-4 guy and yet um those time speeds don't always translate to to real speed, football speed, um the game tape. And so, uh I think I think we're starting to see that now. He's playing he's not thinking as much. Uh he knows what we're trying to do. And so you kind of see that with a number of these guys, as I alluded to before, that have been here for for a little bit of time now that the game's slowing down for him and it allows their abilities to come out. >> What's the biggest level of confidence in Austin Booker that he can elevate his game where he kind of left off last season and what specifically does he have to do in order to accomplish that one? Well, he he's another one that missed some time last year. And so, um I think the more the more time on task we have coaching staff, how we're coaching things, um I I think it's just going to add up. He's still a young player. He's still developing. His body's changed since came in the building a year ago. Um from where we ended the season even until, you know, when he came back in for the spring program, he continues to add more mass. Uh stronger player. um he gets smarter as we go and and uh I I think the coaching is really going to be uh conducive to his style of play as well. So um it's it's reps, reps, reps with all these players, all these young guys. The more reps they get, the better they're going to get. >> Did Dylan take the first game today? >> What's the biggest difference in uh going from being the hunter trying to achieve something and becoming the hunted and in your experience? How have you, you know, what's the biggest struggle that you have teaching that to the team? >> Yeah, I mean, I'm not even really thinking about that right now. We're just, like I said before, we're building our foundation on what the 2026 Chicago Bears are going to look like. That's all we're really focused on. We'll worry about the season, opponents, and all that. Come training camp, end of training camp, we'll start turning the page. But for right now, we're just all about the work. We're all about the grind. We're spending time together. We're getting to know each other. Players get to know players. players get to know the coaches, vice versa. Um, that's what this time of year is for is is putting the work in, bigger, stronger, faster. Um, getting to know introduction to the scheme. Uh, we're not going to master that until we get the pads on. You always fall in love with some players in the springtime and it doesn't always translate. So, you try not to fall in that trap as a coach. We're just we're looking to get a little bit better every single day and and get to know each other in the process. What challenges what challenges are you working through in the run game when you lose Eric Venemy and I mean you have two new starting offensive linemen in that group. >> Yeah. Well, I mean we had several new offensive linemen last year at this time as well. And so um I think that's one of the bigger challenges in our sport is getting five guys to play as one. And that's regardless of how long they've been together. Um all new faces. But, uh, I, like I said before, I think we got a couple of the best offensive line coaches in the business, um, running that operation. A lot of experience, a lot of wealth of knowledge, um, that help help make that transition a little bit better. A guy like Garrett Bradberry, uh, impressed day one just with the level of communication that he brings to the table. He's loud, he's demonstrative. I know that he's going to be able to get all five guys on the same page. Um, but it it is a race. It's a race for us to get to know each other a little bit more and um you saw a year ago it took us a minute before that run game started to get going and clicking and so uh there was a challenge that comes along with that. Along those same lines with the with the running backs and in a new running back coach, you know, coach Studfield's done at a high level for a very long time. He's going to bring a lot to the table schematically once we get into the season, but uh for right now, we're really focused more on our our fundamentals and just getting the tracks down with the backs and and quarterbacks and and the meshes and uh I I think we're going to be in a good spot there. >> Do you think you left a little on the table last season in the offense as far as what Swift could do >> as a receiver? Uh, I mean, we certainly could target him more in the passing game, but, uh, there's probably a number of guys I could say that that for as well, but he's a dynamic player. I've known that about him since since he came into the league, uh, firsthand up there in Detroit and and certainly last year. I I wasn't surprised with the year that he had. Um, is he capable of more? Absolutely. He absolutely is, and he's a vital part of what we do here. >> Ben, um, you said that you were attending more defensive meetings this go around. Um, what have you learned from that process and were you able to make uh certain suggestions and what would those tweaks be? >> Yeah, well, I was in with the defensive staff during during the self scout process and um now that we've turned the page to phase three, the schedule's aligned to where I'm able to sit in with uh their defensive installs and I pick a position room. And so um more than anything, it's it's uh appreciating the level of attention and detail that our guys bring to the table. Um, I think we got, like I said, a bunch of hard workers. They're doing a great job. Right now, our coaches are are are teaching at a very high level, whereas last year we might have, uh, put in a lot of scheme. Now, it's a little bit more fundamental and technique driven, uh, which we feel like is where we need to be this time of year. We'll get to the scheme part later on. Um, but yeah, I mean, it's been really good conversations with with DA and his staff. I think uh, we got a really good group on that side. >> Last one. Ben, it was noted last week that Jaylen Johnson hadn't come to workouts yet. He is here now. That was Yeah. How do you kind of evaluate a veteran like that and that football obsession that you look for in a player? >> Yeah. Well, I mean, voluntary program, so everyone's got uh different ways they want to go about their business. But I I appreciate him being here now with his teammates and and uh getting to know them. We have a lot of new faces in the building. So, um, you can't overstate the the importance of that is just getting to know your buddy because you're going to lay it out on the line for him on on game day. And so, uh, that's that's what we're looking to do right now. >> Where is Gayen in terms of that that best form that he's been looking for? >> The last one. >> Okay. Last one. >> Where's Jayen in terms of that that best form and best health that he's been looking for? >> Um, Jaylen. >> Yeah. >> Yeah. He he just got here, so I don't know. We'll find out. >> Thanks, guys.

I'm really excited just to get going to get this offense progressing. >> Couple more. >> How much of what the way last season did that way last season, how much of that driving you as much your teammates. >> Yeah, every single day. I mean, I I hadn't experienced that in the NFL and uh you know, we we've had a great run of success and you know, we have an objective and goal every single year we step onto the field and for us, we fell short of those short of those goals and so for us it's how do we get back to that winning culture and where we want to be at the end of the year, hoisting the Lombardi Trophy. >> We'll go last three, Pete, Todd, Nick. >> So far, what have you seen from Ken Walker and how do you feel like maybe he's going to boost what you guys are able to do in the game this year? >> Yeah, just being a professional man. uh just hungry to learn, learn our system, just wanting to be great, man. Uh I feel like he has an excellent job and phenomenal job of just going in there going hard. Uh wanting to be taught, willing to be coached, and like I said, I'm really excited to block for him. Um you know, being a former MVP, like it's a really cool thing to be able to have a running back like that. We also have a great running back room in general. You know, D Mart, Charlotte Smith, a couple rookies that we have as well. Uh just phenomenal group of guys. Uh you know, Coach Murray doing a phenomenal job coaching them up, man. It's just an exciting group to be around. I want to ask you about Ken too. Is he is he someone you had watched and admired before? And then can you really get a real feel for what it's going to be like to block for you? >> Yeah, I mean you don't really feel football till it's football. You don't know that until 97 and and training camp at St. Joe's and then the first game of the year and then even a couple weeks on so you start progressing get different feels. But I think it's awesome just the entire group itself. Uh being able to talk to them. I think a big thing is just seeing how they see it. You know offensive line is a cohesive unit. you know, five guys, you know, under the same set of eyes, right? And being on the same page requires reps and time and attention and, you know, over time we'll get that feel. And I'm just really excited about the opportunity. >> Last one. Trey, >> when you went from being a rookie, it's so much about the pre-draft and then feel like you're trying to learn a ton, then you play as a rookie. How much difference is it going from year one to year two? Is that what maybe excites you most about the potential of what Josh is able to do coming back from his own injury at left tackle? >> Yeah. Uh, year one's a blur. You're trying to hold on. Um, but everything's flying at you, man. You go from, you had a whole college season straight into draft prep, and now you're into a whole new organization, a whole new city, a whole new town, whole new group of people, coaches, etc. So, you're really just trying to grasp everything you can while it's going a million miles per hour, and next thing you know, it's over for the first year. But I think the beauty of it is that first year you start to really build up your your football acumen and you know in that second year the game starts to slow down a little bit. So naturally you're going to progress and I I love Josh Simmons man. I love what he's doing. Kingsley Su Matia he's doing a phenomenal job as well and you know the game is going to keep slowing down for him as I get more reps and more actual game experience. So just really excited about their development. Coach heck Andy Mate I mean Andy Kek coach Mate they do a phenomenal job developing players man and it's a great system and they're going to be >> Thanks T. >> Yep. Thank you. Appreciate y'all.

title: Brock Bowers, Tyler Linderbaum, Tre Tucker and Coach Janocko Presser - 5.28.26
text: Hey guys, how we doing? >> All right, here we go. >> Hi, coach. You said that Mendoza's uh mental approach, he's just like a sponge and he even makes coaches think sometimes. How does his mental approach separate him? >> Yeah, I I think that's something we ask from all quarterbacks is just to know the wise behind every play. know the what, know the wise, and be ready to and be ready to uh go above and beyond the X's and O's at times to make things right and to know where guys are at and where they're supposed to be at so that you can help guys knowing not your job but the other 10 jobs as well. >> What has stood out um outside of that? What else stood out to you about Mendoza as he's getting adjusted to the NFL level so far? >> Yeah, I think he's just a he's a guy that wants to come in, grind every day, work. All three of those guys come in every every single day and they they they want to work, they want to learn, they want to be the best in the world. Um he's got two guys ahead of two guys, you know, in the room with him that just set an unbelievable example with the way they work, the way they prepare. Um so he's able to so he's able to see that and grow within himself. >> You talk about the other two guys in the room with him. How important is it to not rush that development in terms of what you guys want that final step to be? Yeah, I I think for us, we're just trying to we're trying to create an environment of competition, trying to create an environment of growth for all three of those guys. You know, no matter where you are in your career, that you feel like you come into that into that meeting room each and every single day and you have a place to grow and learn and become a better player, a better competitor, uh better teammate. >> What's it been like for you stepping up into this offensive coordinator role? Any adjustments in into filling this kind of a role for you? Yeah, I think anytime you move into a into a new position, you have to adapt. But I had a um I've had some really unbelievable mentors. Um you know, the guy sitting in the head chair right now, he and I have worked together closely for the last several years and and years before that. So I've seen him grow and develop, been there step by step with him for that. So been able to to use that knowledge and then use, you know, all the other coordinators been around, have some unbelievable resources on our staff that have been coordinators, that have been head coaches. so able to ask questions, get feedback from that stuff. One of my my first job in the NFL was working for Mike Sullivan when he was the when he was the coordinator. Um, and he's one of the one of the most trustworthy people that you'll ever be around. So, he's been an unbelievable resource for me growing into this role. >> There could have been potentially other opportunities for you. How easy was the decision to come with Mike here? >> I think, you know, sitting there with my sitting there with my wife and we were making a decision the best decision for our family. This was something that we really just we wanted to be a part of. We wanted to be a part of this organization. Want to be a part of building this culture, bringing uh you know, bringing the shield back and um and then getting to work with unbelievable people, getting to work with really good people. That's something in this business that really goes underrated is when you can work with good people, it it makes it makes the job the stresses of the job, the good parts even better and the bad parts um you know, the bad parts you you want to fight through those things with with the people that you're around. John has talked often about a veteran presence is so important for a rookie and in a perfect world the veteran kind of takes the lead and the rookies learns from behind him to start. I mean, are you of that like also? >> Yeah, I think that we have some guy we have some guys in that room that that have played a lot of football that can show roles not just within the quarterback position, but you can see within other parts of the other parts of the room that guys are able to help grow just their position group, but also the offense. So guys that Tyler Linderbomb can come in and you know if a if a young quarterback's cadence is just a little bit off that's that's great insight for him. So all those things we're working together as an offense not just spec specific position groups but all of it. So where we can work there and then we can work as a full offense guys interacting with each other to grow ourselves and using veteran leadership whether it be quarterback um tight end receiver some of those some of those guys that have played a lot of snaps helping younger guys within their position group but with also within the offense. >> How have you seen Kirk being the veteran in that QB room? Not only learning a new playbook and kind of learning the offense for himself, but also taking guys like AOC and Fernando under their wing under his wing. Yeah, I think it's I think it's his his approach to preparation. So, how he takes notes and then just the little tidbits that that he that he shares with the guys and he openly shares with the guys that, you know, maybe this little bit of a a cheat step to your footwork is something that's helped him get his shoulder open to a target, things like that. Uh or um or a memorization thing, how he remembers a certain play or a certain motion. Those are type of those are type of things that he's willing to share and that they help uh whether it's a from a mental aspect or from a physical aspect. >> And for the rookies, a lot is being thrown at him at once obviously, but when you see the confidence level in each one on the offensive side, what kind of stands out to you with these guys and how they're able to just come on the field and play? >> I think as they grow their knowledge base, you see them play faster. So, as they feel more comfortable within the offense, their knowledge base grows, then then you see them play faster. And that's that comes with confidence. So the more that we can immerse them in this system, allow them to grow within it, and then when the picture changes on the snap, if they can just react, that's where you see them, that's where you see them accelerate as players. >> What kind of vision do you have for some of the playmakers like Brock Bowers and Ashton Genty and getting to work with them? >> It's just finding ways to get the ball in your hands. You know, those guys are those guys are talents. They're proven tal, you know, Brock's been a proven talent. Ashton's done a lot of great stuff early in his career. So just finding ways to maximize how and when they touch the ball, finding ways to finding ways to get them open and then maximizing anytime they have the ball in their hands. >> At the end of that, can you just describe Brock Bowers, like his approach to the game? What are some things just your first impression of him that make him different or stand out compared to any other tight end you've worked with? >> Uh he's, you know, I've been I've been blessed to be a part of some great tight end groups and be around some great tight end groups and and Brock certainly fits into that right into into those guys. And you know, when you have a great tight end that that can do stuff for your offense, that can change games, that can change the way you you attack defenses. So, you know, just seeing Brock and his approach, he has that, you know, he has that approach where he's just he just comes to work every single day. And the and the guys around him, same what Mike, you know, all those guys in that room, they just come to work, come to work, come to work. They know what to do, they know how to do it, and then they strive to get better. So, you know, seeing Brock, seeing Mike in that room, those guys, and then lead the rest of the offense, it's something that it's something that that we feel very strongly about and something that as we grow, it's something we hope that that helps to contribute to our success. >> Last week, Coach Kubak said that Mendoza is growing one day to the next. Where have you seen the biggest growth in him? Uh, even though it's early in OTAA? Yeah, I think anytime you come out there, if if there's something that he needs to improve on, he takes that step. Whether it be getting away from center or it be something where, you know, he gets through a progression either too fast or maybe he's a little too slow on stuff. Just uh just creating efficiency for himself in the room or in the classroom, creating efficiency with his mental process or creating efficiency as he as he processes on the field. being able to take what we've done in the classroom to the individual drill. Taking the individual drill, then into the team drill. As you see that apply, that's that's where a quarterback grows. >> What are your thoughts on Caleb uh Caleb Rogers so far? >> You know, he's a he's a guy that keeps working, keeps improving. All those guys, all those guys in that position, it's a really enjoyable room to be around because every day they're helping each other and they really push each other. uh every mo you know in the mornings I love to go in and and see those guys and maybe I can get a joke out of one of the guys but uh they're in there they put in time extra time so you know whether it's Caleb or any of the other guys on the room just seeing just seeing the effort that they're they're putting into growing their mental and physical abilities growing their conditioning all the stuff that that we hope to build through this OTAA period so we can ramp up into training camp >> what's it like to have Tom Brady in the building saw out there practice today and have you picked up anything from him since 201. >> Yeah, Tom's a Tom's an unbelievable resource for us. He's he's u he's been very open. He's somebody that that we can pick up the phone and call or you see him around the building. He's he's you know, he's the greatest of all time. So, getting to be around him every day and any knowledge that you can pick up from him just a great resource to have and something that that was it's very appealing to, you know, sitting in sitting in my chair. >> Where does the listen to your feet moment? Uh that actually that goes back a long way that that's something, you know, we believe in whether it started with the quarterback position, but it really is everything about our offense that that we build ourselves, you know, we build our our brains, then we build ourselves from the ground up. So if you're listening to your feet, whether you're a quarterback and you're progressing on time within your footwork or you're an offensive line and and you're gaining ground on your first step or you're a receiver and what what's my how are my feet helping to contribute to my route depth? All those things. Are we gaining ground on our first step in the wide zone? So everything, you know, our building blocks start there. >> Excitement level for the possibility to play Brock more of more in a receiver role and open the possibility to probably put Michael out there a little bit more. >> Yeah, I think we're just we're going to we're going to get the best 11 on the field whenever we can. We're going to try to, you know, that's what we're using OTAAS for. Uh the way that we can utilize these guys to the best of their abilities. you learning learning ourselves, learning our personnel is something that that we're doing right now. What are the guys, you know, what are the guys route trees? What do they do well in the run game? How are they helping in protection? All that stuff. So, maybe not one thing in particular as far as lining one guy up one place, but just learning the guys right now and how to maximize their ability. >> Best of luck. Clint mentioned a competition between Jack Bash and Dante Thornton. How's that competition going so far? >> Yeah, I think all those guys are competing their butts off. They come every day. They come to work. They put in time, you know, they're st you could tell they're studying at night because they come in with a notebook full of questions. They're always peppering coaches with questions. It's uh, you know, not just those two, but but that whole that whole position group is is exciting because they're guys that that really work hard. >> You obviously have a good relationship with Clint. You guys have worked together a long time, but this is a different dynamic, right? The head coach and OC, I guess. How have you kind of talked about how to approach that part of the new responsibilities and roles that you have? I think that's something we grow with uh grow every day. It's maybe not something that you sit down and write out every single thing, but it's something we grow with every single day. And we have the relationship where we can we can talk about everything. Uh really we talk about anything. Everything we have for for several years. And you know, whether it be X's and O's, whether it be how we're breaking the huddle, whether it be what um Will and Izzy are studying in school that week. Uh but you know they uh you know it's just being having that relationship where we can talk to each other about anything and everything and that's how that relationship grows and evolves. We see something that that needs fixed we fix it whether it be between whether it be between us and our communication or the entire offense. >> Both teams are voluntary. Can you talk about the importance of being able to work with the guys this early and having pretty much everybody that's healthy out there on the field with you? >> I think it's a it's a huge advantage. Credit to our guys. Credit to our guys coming in wanting to wanting to get better and wanting to go compete. So, it's a huge advantage. Not every not every u team and organization is like that. So, we're we're using every single minute. We try to make sure that every single minute that we're with these guys count that we're not wasting a second, not wasting a rep on the field, in the classroom, in the meal room, you know, making sure that that the uh those guys are with with our strength staff. They're maximizing that potential. And our nutritionist, our whole organization's bought into making sure these guys are in the building. We're getting the most out of them. just what's the expectations for Trey Tucker in this offense? >> You know, like all those guys that the entire room, you know, don't want to just single out one guy, but but all these guys maximizing their potential. You know, getting the best out of Trey, taking what he's done good and then maximizing that and then um you know, trying to get spec trying to get specific things for him and every guy to work on coming up with a plan for each guy and how to maximize them, how to get the ball in their hands and what they do once they get the ball in their hands. Just to that point, how does the plan change as you're you're learning about these guys? You watch tape, right, as they come in, but you see them on the field now. How is the coaching staff learning how to use them as as we go on? >> Yeah, I think that I think that's a great question. I think that's something that that we talk about every day about looking at a guy's profile. What does he do well? What is what is he maybe not doing so well? and is that something that we want to change through through a technique or something like that or are we shifting him into a place where he can um where he can thrive better or you know or be in a better place to to succeed. So, it's all a growth process. Each individual person is different, but it's something we're constantly evaluating. Our position coaches do a do a great job of planning out their individual individual uh meetings and their individual periods on the field to maximize maximize those opportunities. Each guy grows his specific skill set so then on he gets into the offense he can uh he can help us succeed. >> We'll do one more Sam. Last one. >> Um you mentioned the experienced coaches that you all have on staff. a lot of guys that have worked with quarterbacks and then you have a veteran like Kirk um who's you know all of you are speaking to a young quarterback in Fernando. How do you make sure that you know you guys are all working in concert together and not you know confusing or getting wires crossed for a rookie? Yeah, I think it's just about it's just about having one singular voice and us being us being all together on it. Whether it's Clint, myself, Sully, you know, any of the guys that that step in that position room, making sure that we have our our wires together that that we're making sure that we give one singular voice, whether it be to Kirk, whether it be to Aiden, or whether it be to Fernando, that when those guys hear that, they understand that there's a clear message, and if it's not clear, we get it fixed right away. Thanks, guys. Thanks, guys. Here we go. What have you uh what's the part of this offense uh that maybe is the produc of what you want to do and how you kind of fit into it? >> Yeah, it's a lot of things, you know. Um we're very multiple. We got a lot of things going on. Um you know, so we can pretty much do anything we want to do at any time, which is great. you know, we just all got to be on the same page and execute. >> What excites you about your role in particular in this offense? >> Yeah. Um, I think Coach Kubak, his big thing is just being able to do, you know, multiple things. Uh, so not just lining up at one spot and playing that spot, but lining up at all three, you know. So, um, in our scheme, you'll see guys everywhere, and that's the whole versatility part. So, I'm excited to do that. Excited to do a bunch of different things. You know, you'll see me here, you'll see me there, you'll see that guy here, there. So, it'll be we'll be all over the place. >> For you, what's what's it like going into year four in the NFL for you? And how maybe things feel different or similar to years past? >> Yeah. Um, I would say a lot more confident. You know, you know, I come in, I know what's expected of me. Um, you know, it's to me it's a 365 thing. I work all year round at this. You know, that's just I what I love to do. So, um, you I I get to come in and work. And now I'm a leader in the room. So, you know, my job is obviously to get the young guys going in the right direction and um going out there and and being the standard. >> What is that like for you kind of being the mentor now among this wide receiver group? >> Um I was very fortunate to have some great guys in my room when I uh when I was a rookie uh which kind of helped me grow and you know as a person and as a player. So that's my whole thing with those guys is how can I make them better you know and how can I help them in any way possible? Like I always tell them my phone's open at any time of the hour because this is what I love to do. So, however I can help them, I'll do it. >> How's it been with Jaylen coming in as well and been making sure he feels comfortable, especially with this team, especially in your guys' group. >> That's my guy. Um, it's been awesome to have him. Um, you know, I watched him from afar. Um, actually in college cuz at the time, you know, I wanted to go to Michigan State. Um, but that's another story. But, uh, he he's he's he's yeah, he's been great, you know, he's another leader in the room, you know, and he's just very smooth. Very smooth, great guy, great leader. Uh, he works hard. Um, and you know, that's that's what expected of him and um, we're very excited to have him here. >> Just what what has been your impression of Clint Kubak and what do you like about like kind of like his straightforward no BS approach? >> I love it. I mean, I'm kind of like that as a person, you know, like let's just get to it. Let's, you know, we're here to win games, we're here to play football. Uh, we want to be connected, you know, that's that's the whole goal. So, um, all the extra stuff, I mean, that's what you do on your outside life, but, you know, when we're here, you know, let's get to work. Let's do what we need to do. Let's win games and let's have fun. And just in regards to Fernando Mendoza, I know it's been early so far. Just what stands out to you about how Mendoza has trying to adjust himself to the infield level. >> I would say his mentality as a rookie is is elite, you know. I mean, it's it's insane, you know, a guy for, you know, where he's been, you know, throughout his career. Um, it's it's insane. And it's also really cool to see. I mean, he was the number one overall pick. I mean, but you you would think that, you know, he comes in as an undrafted guy, the way he works, the way his mentality is, and you know, that's really what you want, you know, for a guy like that. and you know he knows that the expectations are big for him and you know he's got a bright future but he's been tremendous and I'm very excited to work alongside of him. >> How similar or different is he from what you might have seen on TV? >> That's a good question. I mean I would say you know from watching him I mean I think he's everything you know but I would say just for me like I didn't realize how tall he was. He's he's very tall and he's big and um it's cool. So, >> you had a few different offensive coordinators since you've been drafted. How has that impacted you? >> Um, yeah. I I you know, for me, honestly, I've been blessed to be able to learn. You know, obviously, you don't want to have multiple different offensive coordinators. You can't play in the same system, but you know, you can't look at, you know, the negatives. The positives, I was able to learn different schemes, different terminology, um different different things. You know, just seeing different things in a different way. And I think that's helped me, you know, now cuz a lot of things we're doing, I mean, the NFL is the NFL. Everybody runs the same plays. they just call it different. So, you know, the coaching points and you get to learn more. So, I think it's been great for me to learn multiple different offenses and, you know, just to continue to keep improving. >> Said Clint said last week that there's been a lot of competition in the wide receiver room. Do you kind of agree with that? And what do you feel is kind of driving that competition? >> 100% and it should be, you know, um that that's the whole goal, you know, all all the guys, you know, we're all competing, you know, and and that's what's going to make us better, you know. There's no complacency in the room and um all the guys know that and that's what we're out here to do. So, you know, the guys we have in the room, young guys, old guys, we're all competing. We're all trying to go out there and make each other better cuz at the end of the day, you know, we're all going to be out there on the field together. So, um that that's that's our goal and that's what we're going to do. >> Developing chemistry with a quarterback. Is it just reps or is there more to it than that? >> Um I would say it's a little bit of everything. I mean, you get to know guys outside of here, but one of the things that coach Kubak hit on is like being the most connected and I think that's where it comes, you know, and we do a lot of things. So, you know, try to emulate, you know, emulate those things and um that that's really what it is. Obviously, the reps on the field, you'll get that, but you know, obviously I think the the the key is doing stuff outside of here, you know, get really getting to know the person to know the family um you know, because they're your brother, so that's what you do. So, that that's that's the key component to me. What's really been different for me for for you about this off season compared to others in the past considering like the change over and everything that's happened with this team? >> Um, I mean honestly you just you just learn how to adapt, you know. I think for us, for me in particular, like I've been able to have uh the strength staff and their training staff here all four of my years and they've been great, you know. So to have those guys to be here in the offseason to train with AJ and his staff and uh Chris and AJ and all those people like it's been awesome you know to have that uh for me like like I said it's a 365 day thing for me so I'm always working to get better and you know this is the NFL things change every week so just being able to adapt. So >> you mentioned uh you know having an open line during the offseason. Do guys like Dante and Jack take you up on that? Did you get any work in with them or anything like that? >> For sure. you know, in the offseason, it's kind of it's one of those things where, you know, we're with each other so much that, you know, the first couple weeks you're like, "Hey, you know, like you guys go do your thing, you know, you know, relax, rest, you know, a little bit." But definitely for sure, you know, and it's it's more so I would say the mentality part, you know, like how are you seeing coverage or how how are you like what are you doing at this, you know, the physical part like obviously once we get closer to coming back we'll train with each other but people go different places but you know that's the whole thing because I always tell people the game is played 90% here and then 10% you know physically. So um definitely for sure they did for sure. >> Brought up that both of them were competing kind of in this offseason process. How have you seen them kind of drive each other and and grow kind of in this uh in their second season? >> Yeah, I mean that's, you know, they usually say that's when you make your biggest jump. So, both of those guys have been fantastic. Um, we're counting on both of those guys and they know that. I'm just very impressed, you know, cuz I know when I was a rookie and coming into year two, it feels a whole lot different. So, we're going to continue to keep pushing those guys and they're going to keep pushing themselves and we'll see where that goes. middle last season you kind of had to go through this adjustment period where you kind of became you know receiver one overnight with Jakob being you know shipped off and Devonte. What are some things you feel like that you learned from those guys that have made you into kind of the lady you are now and how well do you think you adjusted last year having to become such a more prominent role overnight? >> Yeah, I mean I think those guys you know they really helped me especially Tay and Jacobe as well. Uh it's just the game, you know, whether you say you're the receiver, 1, 2, 3, 8, whatever. Like the number to me that doesn't really matter, you know, you go out there and I'm expecting to make plays, you know, against whoever's guarding me. That's just the mentality of it. So, you know, I would just say it's just the game, you know, but just go out there and put your best foot forward. And um I I remember asking Tay one time like, you know, cuz he had struggles early on in his career. I was like, "What changed for you?" He was like, "When I started blocking the outside noise, you know, that's when, you know, just focusing on the lines." And that's usually really what I've been doing. You know what I mean? Just focusing on that and just focusing on putting my best foot forward. >> It's kind of been your thing since you got here to just, you know, be part of the team, be part of the group, do your job. But you mentioned, I mean, there are people around le oh body one, body receiver two. People assign those things. I guess a lot of receivers in the past have cared about that. Why don't you care? Like why I mean why would you express like, hey, I'm the guy? >> Yeah, because there's 11 people out there on the field, you know, and people always say, you know, do your 11th and that's what I'm out there to do. So, anything else after that, it's not really my concern. You know, as long as I'm doing my 111 and we're in the games, we're having fun, that's all that matters to me. >> Drafted Malik Benson. What have you seen from him as somebody that you share the field with as an offensive player, but also on teams? >> He's going to be a really great player, man. He he he can run all day. He's fast. And uh the the the best thing about him is he's very coachable and willing to learn. He's another guy, like I said, my phone's always open. He's texting me. Um remember, I get into bed very early. I'm getting old. So, uh, he facetimed me and I was like, "Hey man, man, like I'm already in the bed." But, you know, I was able to help him out what he needed and you know that that's all that matters. And like I said, he's going to be a great player. I'm very excited about him. Um, and he's just his willingness to learn, take coaching, and he's going to be a great player. >> What time? >> Oh, man. I'm I'm in bed at 8:30. We got to get up early. So, you know, sleep that's that's the best recovery and it's free. So, got to take got to take advantage of it. >> A couple more. You talked quite a bit quite a bit about Kubak, but on this role for the first time. What have you seen from him? What does he bring? >> Oh, I love him. Very energetic.
