I mean, he one thing about him is he comes in, he's the same every day. His energy is off the charts and that's what you need, you know. Um, obviously Clint, you know, and him, you know, they're very tight and that's just great for us as an offense, you know, so, uh, whenever he says something, we know it's all on the same page and very energetic and he he doesn't miss a beat. Love him. What what's it been like working with Kirk Cousins and how beneficial is it to have a quarterback that has like a good familiarity with like how Kubak was around offense? >> Oh, it's awesome. Kurt's the man, by the way. But, uh, yeah, he um just very smart. Um, you know, he knows the system, you know, so he can kind of like there's things in the system that, you know, he'll be like, "Hey, like on this, this is what I'm looking at." So then you go out there and you do that and he throws you the ball and you catch it and you're like you're on the same page because he knows the system, you know, and he knows defense, he knows coverage and all that. He's one of he's one of the best in the game for sure and he's always been, you know, and um I'm I'm very excited to keep working with him. >> Heading into every new football season, but especially being here the last few years, does it feel different in the building like a newfound optimism or how is that from like a player perspective? >> Oh man, I mean it's it's amazing. you know, we're coming here, like I said, the main thing we're coming here to do, we're not, you know, coming here to really waste time at all. You know, we're coming here to get better, be connected, and win games. And I feel like so far this offseason, we've done all that. You know, we're coming in here, everyone's talking about football, you know, trying to get better, trying to get to know one another. And uh ultimately, so that carries out to the field and then, you know, that way we can, you know, hopefully, you know, execute in the fall and do what it is that we need to do. So, it's been great. And um I'm I'm very very excited for this year. mentioned blocking the outside noise, but do you think this is a wide receiver group that is being underestimated? >> Oh, I mean, you know, honestly, I always think, you know, I I carry a chip on my shoulder and we all should, no matter if we're underestimated, over, whatever it may be. So, for me, I got a chip on my shoulder and I'm going to always be that way no matter what comes, you know. It's like I said, so trying to be the best team player I can be, you know, and I I really just want to win games and have fun. So, all everything else doesn't really matter to me. Awesome. >> Thank you. Appreciate it. Thank you guys. >> What's uh what's what's been the adjustment I guess process for a new team for the first time your career as you're kind of going through this. What's that been like? >> Yeah. Uh it's it's been fun. Uh you know, obviously a whole new staff, whole new playbook, whole new teammates. Just, you know, trying to, you know, blend in with each other and just be the best possible teammate I can be for the guys. And then, you know, obviously figuring out how we, you know, what makes makes us tick, you know, how we operate on a day-to-day basis. And it's been fun to, you know, go through that journey with the guys here. >> How would you assess your acting skills and who was the the best and worst? >> Honestly, me and Colin killed it. First try, they're like, I don't even know if we need to do another one. Um, so I think pretty good. Um, but no, it was fun. Uh, and we were able to do that and hope the fans enjoyed it. >> Do you know if we'll talk about your ability maybe to help often a kid like Fernando Mendoza in terms of whether it's cadence or whatever? Like what have you seen from him in terms of trying to learn how to be a professional quarterback? >> Yeah, he's been he's been great. Uh, you know, soaking in everything everything he's being taught, you know, trying to take it and then apply it into the classroom and onto the field. Um, you can tell, you know, he wants to be great and, you know, that's all you can ask for for these the whole rookie class coming in is how much information can you take in and process and then take it out onto the field. So, as older guys, uh, our job is to help push these young guys along and, you know, they're going to be guys that are going to help us win games on Sunday. So, it's our job to be the best team teammate possible and and help push everyone along. And with that being said, it makes us better as well. What's it been like working with Rick? >> Say that again. >> Working with Rick. >> Oh, okay. Sorry. >> Sorry. >> Uh, Rico. There you go. Uh, it's been awesome. Uh, tons of experience and, you know, all the coaches in there with Mario and Ben, uh, just, you know, really pushing us to be the best versions of ourselves on the field and then in the classroom. Uh just with Rico's experience, you know, he's coached a lot of football and it's it helps with a room like ours just, you know, trying to gel together and get as much information from him as possible. You know, just the way he communicates and and goes about uh football, it, you know, resonates with us. >> What's the communication process been like between you and the quarterbacks that you've been working with? How important is it for a young guy like Mendoza and really get that communication going? Yeah, I think that's the the biggest part of it is just whenever I think it's the whole align and quarterback has to, you know, work in one and and see see the same things together, whether that be protection, run game, and it's, you know, obviously center quarterback job to communicate with each other and be on the same page. So, just having that dialogue is big with whatever quarterback's in there with us, uh, is important and it's it's only going to build a stronger connection and get better as time goes on and as we get more reps. But um you know happy with how we're you know moving along and and processing everything. >> You talk about joining a new team and new coaches new scheme for the first time. How do you can you talk a little bit about what your job is as a center in this Clint Kubak offense? >> Yeah. Um no I think I think it's most important is just communication. I think that's everywhere. you know, center's job communicating, you know, being a leader on that offensive line and trying to get people in the right places and communicate as loud and effectively as possible. And then on the flip side of that, you know, having communication with the quarterback, uh, making sure everyone's on the same page and, you know, seeing it in the same lens. And, you know, as we move along, you know, continue to, you know, learn the offense as a unit. Um, and then, you know, we'll get closer and closer to where we want to be. Um, but we're we're a long ways from that and we just got to keep getting better. >> Tyler, you uh blocked for Derrick Henry for a number of years. What stands out early on about Ashton Genty? >> Yeah, I think, you know, one, you in this time period, you see how people work. Um, it's, you know, obviously hard to get an idea of everyone's skill set on the field with no pads or live bullets, but, you know, just seeing a Ashen work and and how he goes about his day, his operation, um, how he wants to get better, you know, that's what you appreciate out of a young guy, and I think he's a guy that's obviously going to have to play a big role in our offense this year. Um, and, you know, we're excited for him. >> What has been your impression of Clint Kubak as a coach and kind of like his little his straightforward, no BS type of mentality? >> Yeah. Um, I think as players, you know, you don't want things, you know, you don't want any gray area. You know, you want things to be black and white. And I think coach Kubak does a good job of that. You know, his expectations, you know what they are. And if you're not meeting his expectations, uh, then then you understand that. And I think, you know, as players, it's our job to, you know, uphold the standard that he has in place and then, you know, continue to push each other and push others around you. But, you know, it's been awesome to work with coach Kubak and the whole coaching staff, you know, trying to, you know, get his message out to the players. It's been fun. >> What's it like having Tom Brady out there at practice today and having him in the building? And have you been able to interact and pick anything up from him since joining the team? >> Uh, no. I haven't had really any conversation with Tom, but you know, obviously, you know, the GOAT, so have a guy like that in the building. You know, I'm you know, I'm sure the quarterbacks are using him a lot, too. just, you know, you know what they see and how he can help out. But, you know, having a a mind like that in the building is is nice to have. >> Is there a lot of adjustments that you have to make going from quarterbacks that are very mobile like Lamar, Snoop, Cooper, and then going now to the situation you're at with guys that are a little more traditional like her, Fernando, Aiden, and do you adjust right now or is that something you got to wait until the pads come out in training camp? >> Um, good question. Uh, no. I think, you know, at the end of the day, football's football. Um, there's always going to be, you know, extended plays no matter who the quarterback is. Um, might happen more with other quarterbacks um than others, but at the end of the day, you know, as offensive lineman, your job is to block the guy in front of you as long as possible and however long that takes. So, that's that's that's my approach. That's how the offensive line's approach has to be. You know, if it's if it's a quick pass, we can't bank on the ball getting out fast because you never know. It's a game of football. So there's a lot of broken plays in this league and you know sometimes things don't go as planned. So your job is to block the man in front of you as long as you can. >> The the specific act of like snapping. Is there a difference in the way quarterbacks want it or is your job just to do the same consistent snap every time? >> No, I think you trying to be as consistent as possible whether under center or in shotgun. Um, you know, it's it had it once you work with a quarterback so often, you know, everyone has their different, you know, feels and stuff like that. But, um, it's just, you know, building that cohesiveness cohesiveness with each other, um, is important. >> Talk about all the changes that you've made, you know, coming to a new building, but also you have to, you know, joke on the West Coast for the first time. You just got married a few weeks ago. You know, what was that like? And also, you know, how much has that been kind of been trying to combine all of that within one off seasonason of signing with a new team and doing all that? What has that been like? >> Yeah. Um, it's been awesome. You know, very blessed, uh, you know, to be in the position I am obviously getting married. Um, you know, best best weekend of my life. Uh, and then, you know, obviously being able to come to a new team. Um, you know, just start of a new journey. Uh, you know, I've always been a guy that just, you know, attacks each and every day. Um, you know, attitude and effort is the most important things and that's the things I hang my hat on. So, just excited to be here, be with a new team and give as much as I can possible, you know, to be the best version of myself. >> Going back to the the snapping stuff, but so much was made of Fernando not taking a lot of under snaps in college and how he's adjusting that in the NFL. How much of that is kind of on you or how much have you taken on you to be like this is how it's done to kind of help him along in that process? Yeah, I think with that it just comes with reps. Um, obviously if you don't have many reps with it, the more reps you get, the more comfortable you get. Um, and obviously he's not the first quarterback ever to not, you know, have a lot of reps under center. So, it's just the more reps you can get with the, you know, with all the centers is is important and, you know, this is the perfect time to, you know, get that done and then obviously moving into fall camp and into the season to where it doesn't become an issue. Coming from Baltimore, you're, you know, you're accustomed to strong tight end play with Mark Andrews and I can say likely just what's it been like being teammates with Brock Bars th this far and just what have been your and what has stood out to you about him? >> Yeah, Brock's awesome. Brock's got like that, you know, killer mindset in him, you know, doesn't talk much, just goes out there and works. Um, I'm surprised you guys even get him in here to talk, but uh, no, he's been awesome. No, just seeing guys like that, you know, breath of fresh air. Just how they operate, how they go about their business. It it's you want guys like that on your team and that's what you appreciate. >> And just like uh looking at Kubak staff uh with Janokco, Rico, these are guys that are just familiar with what he wants and are from previous experience. I was just wondering how beneficial has that as a player to have so many guys in the coaching staff that knows like exactly what Clint Kubaka wants and have a straight like a straightforward approach and their goals and has for the team. >> Yeah, I think it's huge. Um, you know, we got to, you know, obviously new staff, bunch of new players, you got to build a culture and, uh, to have coaches and players that are familiar with that and with how he wants to operate, that's that's big. um you know because at the end of the day we don't got many practices before the first game um when you look at the big picture. So how fast can we you know get the message uh and then understand how he wants to go about our business and how he wants us to operate and it's our jobs as you know players to to uphold that standard and you know at the end of the day uh you know we're excited for the opportunity but you know have to have a sense of urgency as well. uh you know to get that message and then and then put it onto the field. When >> it comes to building a cohesive offensive line, you mentioned earlier that you guys have a long way to go as you guys are trying to fit see which pieces fit where. What are some major steps that you guys have taken so far this early that are kind of pushing you towards that right direction? >> I think you know just the reps on the field that's the most important thing. uh you know obviously not a lot of us have played with each other so it's just understanding how we see things our communication you know obviously new terminology new playbook so it's just the more reps that we can get in a team setting um in a group setting you know the better off we're going to be and you know that's what I mean just a long or a lot of work to do um because at the end of the day you're never going to you know be 100% where you want to be you know just have to have that mindset to continue to work and continue to get better saw the O line and Fernando and and Kirk get the Golden Knights game on Thursday on Tuesday I think. um just how has this group kind of built camaraderie in the locker room, off the field, that kind of thing? >> Yeah, I think you know you want to build those connections. Obviously, a lot of new faces the more you know obviously you have a personality in the building and then you know you want to get to know guys outside the building. So obviously Vegas is a great place for that. A lot of things to do. The Knights are killing it. Um so just more opportunities that you can get a group of guys together um learn learn about each other, you know, the better it's going to be. Tyler, what has JPJ left playing besides you so far and on the field? >> Yeah, he's been great. Um, you know, Jackson's a guy that you can tell he loves football, plays the game the right way, and just wants to get better each and every day. And, you know, those are the kind of guys that you want on a team. Those are the kind of guys that you want on the O line. So, um, love his mindset, love how he how he approaches each and every day. Uh, and, you know, excited to work with him. >> In what way specifically do you hope to impact the offensive line? How would you explain what it is that you bring? >> Yeah, I think, you know, just one being myself, you know, and at the end of the day, you know, it's it's my job to get everyone to be on the same page. Uh, you know, to play at a standard that we we set and that we want to play at. Um, and us collectively as a unit, you know, we decide how we want to play. It's it starts in practice. It starts in the meeting rooms on what it we want it to look like. Um, you know, and if we're falling short of that, that's on us. So, you know, the more we can, you know, practice how we want to practice, play how we want to play, the better off we're going to be as a unit and the better this offensive unit is going to be. >> You guys good? >> Oh, thanks. >> Thanks, guys. >> Thank you, >> Brock. Last year you kind of you dealt with especially the first time of the season you dealt with like the knee injury just you know going into this year. How how are you feeling from a health standpoint? >> No, I feel great. I mean it feels good to be back out there um practicing full speed, you know, getting back into football with all the guys again. So um I mean I had a good offseason working out um staying healthy and um you know trying to get back to 100%. >> Have you ever been called a football robot from heaven before your thoughts when you heard that? >> No, that was the first but uh no it was uh I guess it's a compliment. So, it's it's it's pretty funny. It's pretty funny. >> Did you like it? >> I guess it's compliment, right? I don't know. I That's how I took it. So, >> what did your teammates say? >> They thought it was funny, too. They were all like um you know, poking fun of me and stuff. So, it was good. >> What's your relationship been like with Clint? And, you know, he kind of give you those gleanings that these are things that he's thinking about you and terms of having met you and working with you. >> Yeah. No, I mean, he's he's very serious, you know, all about football, which which I like. I mean, he's I mean, he's all about ball in the meetings. He just doesn't, you know, u doesn't mess around. So, I I like that a lot. So, um definitely is going to help us out in the locker room. >> You said that there was going to be a lot of versatility in your guys' offense. Something Kubak really wants to implement. How excited are you for that? >> No, I'm really excited. I mean, I mean, just open up the offense and let it roll. I mean, we got some really talented dudes out there, so I'm I'm excited to see what happens this year. >> What's your first impressions of Fernando Lendoza so far? >> Yeah, you know, he he's a great guy. He's a great guy to have in the locker room and you know being a rookie quarterback it's a lot of stuff mentally. So I think he's been doing a really good job at that and um you know really being involved in you know like the playbook and um just learning as much as he can as fast as he can. So I think he's done a really good job at that. >> Earlier in practice today you know you caught a touchdown from Kirk and and team Fury. You know what was that like kind of having that chemistry with him and what about him as a quarterback makes him so good working with him? >> Yeah you know he's a veteran guy so he's seen a lot of stuff and uh I mean working with him you know he throws the ball. He's been around the league a while. So, um, yeah, he's just a great QB. I mean, it's hard to it's hard to find too many things negative about him. >> Where are you at physically right now as you're going through OTAAS and and how difficult was last year to not be able to do what you wanted to do all the time. >> Yeah, I like I said, I feel great right now. I mean, I feel like 100% ready to roll. Excited for the season. And, uh, I mean, yeah, last year was frustrating. You know, first game kind of, uh, banged up my knee a little bit. So definitely wasn't um how I planned my second year to go, but no little adversity and um you know, just got to come back stronger >> Are there points of uh you know, do you find any points of emphasis you want to improve on as a player, even as a leader? Anything heading into year three in particular? >> Yeah. Um you know, I think just just honing in on my game and every single part of it like I mean even staying healthy too. I've been trying to do a lot more um you know like preventative um you know work like trying to stay healthy throughout off season and um going into camp especially and going into the season you know you got to that's half the battle is staying healthy and staying available week to week. Um and other than that you know just trying to perfect little things like you know releases route running uh blocking techniques. So all all the stuff. Clint said last week that this offense has to get most out of you. Kind of what do you feel that looks like for you in this offense? >> Yeah. I mean, I think I can be a pretty versatile uh player. So, I I mean, I can I feel like I can do a decent amount of stuff. So, I mean, it's just kind of however they want to use me. So, I'm I'm ready for whatever they want me to do. >> You talk about however they want to use you based off the film. You see, you know, what they did in like in Seattle with Barner, you know, those other guys. What are some things that really excites you about this system when you try to learn it? Yeah, I mean like I mean you saw everyone saw the success they had last year. So I mean we're just trying to um you know see what they did well and take it from there and try to build it into our own our our own offense and uh make it our own. So we got a bunch of great guys here and we'll see how we'll see how it goes. >> When it comes to building chemistry with the quarterback, is it just reps or is there more to it? >> Yeah, I think a lot of it's reps. I mean, they got to know um kind of what you're thinking when you're running the route, you know, talk talking through it afterwards in film and um and just I mean, just throwing the ball and catching the ball. I mean, uh I think the QB just needs to see the way certain guys move and um you know, just get connected that way. >> You you talk about going over film like after after practice, you go through drafts, things like that. Have you noticed Fernando kind of asking the right questions and is that like something be encouraging as you kind of communicate with him? Yeah, you know, I mean, like I said, he's trying to uh take it all in and um you know, they have all those rookie meetings after practice, so they're all they're all swept into those. Um so, I mean, um I'm trying to think of an example, but no, I mean, he's been he's been great. I mean, me, like I said, mentally he's all there and he's he's all in. >> Brock, whether on the field or off the field, what has been the biggest change you have noticed this offseason compared to offseason past? >> That's a good question. I mean it's it's hard to say. I mean I feel like um we have a lot of urgency this year, you know. Um that's um a big thing kind of focus I think is uh being urgent in everything we do and really trying to hone in and get better at everything we do. >> You talk to Tom at all or you know picked his brain about what Grock did with him or or has he offered that up at all? And like have you found yourself talking to him more heading into this season and the beginning of this off seasonason than in the first two years? >> Yeah. No, he's definitely been around more and um I mean he's he's a resource anytime we need him. So I mean it's really good to have I mean that kind of guy around, you know. I mean uh like the goat. So I mean it's it's great to have him around and be available with any question we have. >> You think there's any more acting in your future after the US brothers? >> No, probably not. It was pretty it was brutal. It was brutal. Thanks. Good. Thank you guys. Appreciate it.

title: Matthew Stafford Talks Contract Extension; Sean McVay & Puka Nacua On OTAs & Rookie Class Progress
text: Welcome back, >> Matthew. How's it been going out there and what's new? >> Uh, it's been going good. Um, it's fun to be out there again. Obviously, long break after the season and and fun to be back out running around with the guys and and uh just seeing everybody's face again, getting in the in the huddle. Um, you know, playing a little bit of football again. So, it's been fun. >> How are you feeling? >> I feel good. Body feels good. um throwing it, throwing it like I know how to throw it and and uh you know for for somebody my age feel pretty good. >> What what pleased you the most about what you saw? >> Oh man, I don't know. We just this time of year is just you know how do we break the huddle? How do we what do our fundamentals look like out there? Um you know obviously you want to go out there and make plays. We have no pads on. It's seven on seven. We're jogging through some of our team stuff. So, uh, limited expectations in the, you know, how the result of the play is, but hey, what does it look like when we break the huddle? How do we feel about our fundamentals, our assignments, all those kind of things, that's what you're looking for. Testing yourself mentally a little bit, obviously physically out here as well, staying sharp. But, um, this is a, you know, getting to know each other, getting to compete with each other, learning how to practice, you know, time of year. >> How exciting you to, uh, get your extension signed? >> Uh, it was good. You know, I obviously, uh, you know, have a a ton of respect for for our team and our organization. um you know, happy to uh you know, have your have next year taken care of if and you know, if I decide to play and and uh you know, they still want me back, but uh no, just just excited to get that behind me cuz I just want to come out here and play and and not think about that kind of stuff. So, great to get that done uh you know, sooner rather than later. >> The expectation the expectation is still to go year to year as you kind of consider your future. >> Yeah, I think so. With these, you know, that's the conversations that I've had with the team. Obviously, if I'm feeling healthy and uh you know, it's like I said, it's it's a family decision. I can't sit there and tell you what it's going to look like 365 days from now. If you can, let me know. But uh you know, it's just one of those deals where I'm I'm doing uh you know, the best I can to make sure that I can play as long as I can and and uh make sure that my family and and I uh you know, are all on the same page before we you know, embark on whatever season it may be. Matthew, when you have a a young quarterback like Todd Simpson and you have a has such admire admiration for you, uh he refers to you as an assassin um on the field. When you have a young quarterback like that, how do you guys continue to build the rapport, build the chemistry, and obviously teach him certain things and have him absorb what you teaching him? >> Yeah, no doubt. I think my job first and foremost is to get myself and our team ready to play as best I possibly can. He's a part of that team. There's no question about it. We're in a unique position in the fact that we play the same position. I have a ton of experience and he's just now starting his journey as an NFL player. So, listen, I know he's going to watch uh not only me but other guys, you know, and Stson who's been around a little bit too and and really just soak up as much coaching as he possibly can. He's a guy that asks questions. I've been trying to answer those as honestly and as thoroughly as I possibly can. Um he's a smart kid. He's got talent. Obviously, he's um you know, a high draft pick. So, um happy to add good players to our team. He's one of them. Uh, but my job is, you know, go out there and get myself and our team as ready to as ready to play as I possibly can. >> Sean said that contract Sean said that he uh talked to you before they made the Tyson pick. What was your reaction and what was that conversation like? >> I'm not going to get into too much to what our conversation was. I appreciate him talking with me about those kind of things. Um, we have constant dialogue um and a great relationship. So, I appreciate that. Um, I understand where the team's coming from. Listen, I'm not 25 years old and I and I get that. Um, so we're doing everything we can to be as good a football team as we can for now, for the future, for for all of it. >> How much does it help you when you know your teammates are depending on you for for literally everything on and off the field? >> Uh, no, I I I think at the quarterback position, um, you know, you're inherently, you know, pushed into a leadership position. Obviously, I've been doing this for a long time, and I try to be myself as best I can. I feel like that's the best way to lead is is to be authentic in who you are. Um, I feel like hopefully the guys know that about me and and um I I know I have a ton of experience, so I'm going to try and help every way I can, but at the same time, I'm still learning. I'm talking through things with Devonte or with Puka or with other guys, too, and just trying to see it through their lens as well. So, um, you know, be great part of being a leader is is, you know, having that communication, and communication to me is a two-way street. So, I'm always trying to share knowledge, but also listen and learn as well. eventually with all of your girls with you when you did sign your deal. What's that like year after year now that they're kind of getting to be an age where like do they understand? >> Yeah, they do. Um they do. Uh I mean to a certain extent, you know, um uh but it's the best. Uh it's my favorite part of Sundays, you know, is getting shoot, we play every day of the week this year, I feel like, but uh of game day, I should say. Um, so, uh, it's just being with them and getting to getting to hang with them and watching them, you know, learn to enjoy this game and and everything that comes with it. Um, you know, the team aspect of it, the toughness mentally, physically, all that is such great learning tools. And, um, they just get excited. They get excited to come cheer on our team. As much as they cheer for me, I don't know if you guys are at away games, but they're cheering for the defense like crazy out there. I'm like, "Oh, I can hear them all day." So, it's uh, it's fun to watch them do their thing. and and I wouldn't be doing this if they weren't excited about it and uh wanting to come, you know, to practice the games to to cheer me on. So, um their support means the world to me. >> Wondering what your reaction was when you first saw the schedule come out separate from Australia. Uh cuz that first month could be pretty brutal, right? Come home, have one game, and then mile high and back east. >> Yeah, I'm still trying to figure it out to be honest with you. Um there's a lot of moving parts, but you know, it's kind of cliche, but we're just so trained to, okay, what's right in front of us? You know, I mean, everybody looks at the big picture and goes, "Oh, you know, week 14 or 15 or 16." And we're going week one, you know, and and really Thursday OTA today, you know, and and uh cuz we drive ourselves crazy um trying to figure out what's going to be the best, what's our approach going to be, how are we going to do this, that, the other. Hey, listen. You guys tell us where to be, how to work. We'll go out there and do it and uh you know, show up on whatever day of the week it is. Go out there and play and try to try to win ball games. >> Yeah, that's right. Put the ball down. >> Feeling good physically with all the years you have under your belt. Is there anything you did in the offse? >> Not so much different than I did last year. Just trying to as I as I get older, as I accumulate years and and miles on the tires, I guess. Um just try to listen to my body as best I can. um figure out what maybe needs a little tweak here or there, but uh it it was pretty similar to what I did last year and and uh you know, hopefully can feel uh really good all the way leading up into the season. >> What's it like having Brian Allen and Robert Woods out there as coach? >> It's great. Um my high school coach was Coach Allen. So, every time I see Brian, I say, "Coach Allen." He goes, "Player." But, uh uh it's fun, man. old teammates that are coming back, giving back to the game, learning um seeing what it's like to be a coach and and those guys are going to bring great knowledge both like in the schematic part of it, but also um you know, just the the humanity of playing the game, right? Like they've done it and uh I think that's really valuable both in the you know over there on this side of the building where the coaches are and in the meeting rooms, but also out on the field too, talking after plays with a receiver if it's Woody or with an O lineman if it's BA. So, um it's fun to to have played a bunch of football games with all those guys and then um you know, have him be our coach as well. It's it's pretty cool >> with all that has gone through during the offseason. Have you had any conversations with him about navigating through that and how does he how's he looked out here during >> I think he's looked fantastic. Uh you know, happy for him and happy for um you know, his success to get back out here and just play the game he loves. And um as far as conversations, absolutely. I I'm talking non-stop to him. Um he's a great person, great kid, and and just doing everything I can to try and um you know, give advice when it's needed or or also just be his buddy, too. So, um you know, I think uh I'm I'm doing everything I can I think everybody is to just support him because he's such a special person on our team. Uh great player, great person, and and we're happy that uh you know, he's back doing his thing. >> In regards to your in regards to your extension, just from the outside, it seemed like a more straightforward, quiet process than a year ago. Like do you feel like at this point you've chosen whenever the day comes to finish your career with the Rams? >> I'm not going to sit there and and try to uh predict the future. That's two for you trying to make me predict the future. But uh no, I I I'm if I was uh that would probably be a yes, but I'm not going to put anything. I mean, this is football. Um this is the world. This is life. I don't know what's going to happen. But um I do love playing here. I love playing for this organization. Love my teammates. Uh and my family loves it here. talking very much about today's Twitter stand. At what point did you say, "Okay, the disappointment of last year is behind me and now is a new start." Or have you have you hit that? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, to me that happens pretty pretty quickly. Um, you know, obviously you want to win every game. You want to be the last team to win the last game of the year. That didn't happen. Uh, but I still have a ton of appreciation for what we accomplished, how we played, how we went about our business. Um, there's only one team that's happy at the end of the year when it comes to wins and losses, but can you take something from it? And there's no question in my mind that myself, my teammates, everybody was in that group can take a lot from that year. Um, and so I appreciate it for what it's worth. Um, and I move on. You know, I think that's the way we all are. I haven't heard really anything talked about when it comes to last year. We're a new team, a new group. We've got new players, new coaches in a lot of spots as well. So, this is a how fast can we get to know each other? How well can we gel as a group and go attack this year? Um, that's our mindset. That's my mindset. And I think that's going to serve us well. How do you like this team basically having the bullseye on its back this year? Even though you didn't win the Super Bowl last year, you have the most prime time games. You are the Super Bowl favorite, I guess, in the in the betting ranks. All the attention is on the Los Angeles Rams coming into this season. >> Uh, that doesn't really concern me or my teammates or our coaching staff to be honest with you. team up the road in Seattle won the Super Bowl. So, they uh you know, they are obviously the team to beat, but uh we're just doing everything we can to try and as be a good be as good a football team as we possibly can be. Like I said, we've got some new pieces on the defensive side of the ball, a bunch of returning guys on offense. How can we become better? You know, how can we find ways to win those games that we lost last year, um and make our, you know, make our season the success that we want it to be? But we're not worried about any outside expectation. I know I'm not. Um and I know our team isn't. And that's led by Shawn and our group up front. >> Has Sean been clear to you? >> Has Sean been clear to you that you'll play for as long as you want to be here? >> Uh yeah, I mean I think so. Uh as long as I do my job at a high level, uh you know, that's everybody here, right? You can't just sit around and play terrible and you know, they're not going to just keep bringing you back. Um so you got to go out there and play well and and you know, be the best option at your spot. So yeah, that's that's my uh that's my goal. Matthew, as you talk about the family being part of the decision for whatever length of time you're going to play, how how much more fun is it just having your daughters being there, understanding it, enjoying it, and you want to share everything with them as long as possible? >> Yeah, it's great. Um, you know, Kelly does an unbelievable job of getting them to to most, if not all the games, and and having Kelly and and my girls there means a ton to me. I love uh, you know, sharing this experience with them. It's really unique. I don't take it for granted, you know, for the opportunity that I have to do what I get to do for as long as I've been able to do it. And being able to share it with them, uh, you know, means the world. >> Last month, last month >> coaching them, it's been awesome. It's been a lot of fun. Uh, super proud of him. We have a bunch of great, you know, great girls and boys on the team. Um, I kind of got thrust into the into that spot. We were supposed to be a high school kid coaching him. He kind of bailed, so I was like, everybody kind of looked at me like, "Hey." And I was like, "All right." Um, sure. I'll go for it. But, uh, it was a lot of fun. I I tried to keep it light, teach them the fundamentals, but also just let's go have fun and and enjoy this game and and they did a great job. >> Going to playing another season with Devonte, has there been any conversation with you two being pretty more prominent bets together? And just what do you anticipate that being like? >> Yeah, no, I'm excited. Um, obviously had a really good, you know, first season with him. He was ultra productive, ton of touchdowns, bunch of yards and catches, and and I think there's even another level to it for myself and for him. So, um, just excited to continue to get those reps and, uh, that understanding. I feel really lucky to play with a player like like Devonte that, uh, you know, has done it at a high level for such a long time. Um, I don't take that for granted. He is a special player, special human being. >> Thanks. >> Welcome. >> Hello. >> How you doing? >> Doing great life. Uh, it's been uh, a busy offseason, but it's been good. Nice to be back in football and be around a bunch of the guys. What have you learned the most about yourself on and off the field and how do you continue to maintain that positivity and and then basically having your teammates really rally around you and really, you know, encourage you and elevate you? >> Yeah, I'd say in this offseason I've been really grateful for the support um from the organization, especially my teammates. Uh people reaching out at different times of the offseason. Um just checking in um one checking in how I'm doing, see how my family's doing um with with my with my son growing up as he is. Um, so I'm I'm just really grateful for the people around me and in this organization and uh some of the things I feel like I've learned is it's okay to ask for support and then uh to to recognize the the platform that that I have and uh being a professional football player and trying to use that for uh for the betterment of myself and for those around me and the people that have supported me. >> There were some allegations made against you regarding New Year's Eve. Just what were your what was your reaction to what the other party alleged happened? um with it being an an ongoing legal battle um out of respect for for the other party involved uh don't really have have much to speak on but uh uh like kind of just previously stated a moment for me to learn um from kind of some of the situations I was putting myself in and then uh also having just an awareness of uh how I'm conducting myself in and out of this football field. he'll come up with >> everything that's happened during the off season. What have you learned about yourself and what you can do to make yourself even better? >> Um like I I was like um especially asking for for support um seeking out help from uh from trusted individuals in my group of circle and then uh uh therapy is something that I've started um learning to to trust those around me and to to find ways to work out through some of the things that I find difficult and uh are are stressors in my life. Did you feel like a a younger version of yourself couldn't ask for help? Was this a a small hurdle or a huge hurdle? >> Um, I'd say a little bit of a big hurdle. Um, having coming from a big family and just being involved in sports is kind of always uh you get knocked down, there's one bad play, there's another play to kind of to get ready to prepare and kind of make that that correction. And uh never just uh yeah, seeking seeking assistance. And uh there was there's always been good people around me, but always something where it's like, man, the the wrongdoings or the mistakes I made felt like it was like an internal thing and never allowing that to really express. I like to think of myself as a pretty happy, outgoing guy and uh enjoying life, but uh there also were some of the difficulties of just uh being in the this professional sport and just throughout my entire life. >> Did you do that yourself or was there someone who gave you a nudge along the way? uh something that uh I think recognizing for myself of kind of where I was at uh but definitely had some uh some people in my my inner circle who who encouraged me to go out there and uh find ways to improve myself. >> Is that are you an ongoing program or is that just a short >> uh I um it was I guess a short stint I've continued uh working I I work with our our team uh therapist over here and then continuing some of those meetings weekly. Uh I feel like it's something that improved. Uh little did I know that uh even just writing in a journal has been as simple as that and just finding ways to express some of the things that I I find near and dear to my heart and then also just to write down the the accomplishments. There's been a lot of good things in uh amidst of some of these things that have been challenging for me. But uh it's been it's been a great improvement in my life. >> For as much as you've accomplished individually, why is it important to remind yourself those accomplishments in this process? >> Um I think now looking at them like it's crazy. I'm I'm getting ready to turn 25 tomorrow. Um, but uh I I I have I have a young son and to think of uh the things that I I have the opportunity to share with him uh in the the great things I've able to accomplish and uh to enjoy those moments, but then also to teach him in some of the mistakes that I've made. So, there's an opportunity for him to learn before some of those uh uh wrong decisions can be made. >> What has Sean communicated to you just in regards to how he wants to see you move forward from these incidents? >> Yeah. uh coach uh I feel like since since I've been here obviously I think one of the things that he says is to be a world-class communicator and that's something I think from the moment I've stepped into this building to to just barely walking off this football field uh he's always been right there to to support me and it it's been great we've had uh many conversations um about me being a father about me being a football player and just puka the person so I'm I'm very appreciative of coach always being there in my corner and uh especially on my goes out to my teammates and this organization as well >> you talk about a few of the new faces is in the room and uh how it's affecting so far and it's very early but just what they bring to the squad. >> Yeah, I feel like uh specifically for our room CJ's come in and been great. Uh he comes in and is asking the right questions. He's he's taking notes and uh when the opportunity for him to answer some of the questions in the meeting and and to show that that he's understanding this knowledge, he's been really great at that. So, it's been fun and uh I think it's been a testament to I think the veteran in our room at Dvonte and and an opportunity for me to continue to learn some of the new things that are getting implemented and then continue to share that information that I've absorbed from our coaches, from Matthew and uh and just playing football at this level. So, uh sorry, he he's been he's been great and then for for Ty Simpson to get the opportunity to be in in the quarterback room. Um it's been great for to to see the same thing. Uh it's a it's a a lot in our offense to be able to come in and uh at that position to understand all the things that are going on, but uh I think we have he has the best in the world, the reigning MVP to go in there and ask questions and uh our coaching staff in that room has been great in being able to uh communicate in the ways that he can learn >> through the off season. Um where does kind of your contract situation fit in in the grand scheme of things? >> Um I'm not not not too sure. Um I I know that uh my job is to come up here and uh to be with the guys and go out there and compete every single day. And that's been kind of my mindset. Um if I can continue to improve as a person, uh I know that uh the coaches and the people around me are helping me improve as a football player. So those are the things that I can control and then uh hopefully allow those other things to to handle themselves. >> Are you comfortable playing in 2026 without an extension? >> Yeah, I I haven't really really thought about it. I'm like I I I enjoy playing football. Um it's been the the biggest dream come true. So, uh, to be able to be out here and play for this organization specifically has been, uh, has been awesome. I I couldn't imagine myself playing anywhere else, but it's been fun to go out here and, uh, be around these guys. And, uh, hopefully, yeah, like I said, I let all those things handle themselves. >> You do think about when you do think about the contract and what could be out there for you, what do you feel like, I guess, you need to show or need to do to, you know, be able to, you know, achieve your dreams and, you know, show to this team or another team, you know, that you're worthy of that kind of major deal. Um, I think continuing in in these uh habits and routines that I've established for myself and uh this this offseason and I feel like some of the things that I've established and being this going into year four of the NFL. Um, consistency, the physicality I feel like I play the game of football with is something that I pride myself in and uh I don't see that kind of changing anytime soon. Um, but then the ability to understand and develop as a wide receiver. I I would say I've been blessed to to have I think two of the best at the wide receiver position mentor me and be out there on the football field with me. So, uh, as much as I feel like I've had success, there's always room to improve. So, uh, looking at the things that I can do better, um, minimizing those drops, uh, becoming better at the top of the routes and at the line of scrimmage, and then, uh, the physicality, uh, that's a mindset thing I think, uh, is is something that pretty deeply instilled in my brain. >> Quick question. What kind of teammate you try to be during OTAAS? >> Um, I think it I feel like try to be somewhat of a rookie again. come back in there, reset the the mindset and uh understand I'm like, man, we're coach does a great job of starting kind of at the the basics and the foundation so we can all develop and uh understand uh the intent of some of the things that are going on, but then also use some of the the knowledge and the experience that I've had in playing this game and give it out to the new guys in the building and then also share uh some of the things that work for me. Everybody's got different body types and moves in different ways and uh so just communicating uh try like coach says, try to be a world class communicator. >> Thank you. Appreciate it. What's up, man? >> Oh, guys, go ahead. >> Coach, how do you how would you describe what you saw today from a from just a general standpoint? >> It was good. You know, I mean, it's been good to be able to just get back out here. There's obviously limitations, Jim, in terms of what we can do right now, but the engagement, the communication, you know, our operations on both sides and um some of the things that we can do to compete a little bit has been a real positive. But I re I really just like the overall vibe from our players, from our coaches, taking it one day at a time. Um, you know, but today was a positive day for us. >> How did it feel to get Matthew's extension done and come to the TAS with that? >> It was good, you know, and he and we've had really good dialogue all throughout um, you know, really just in general. Um, and so it was it was a very u, you know, a good positive thing went in the direction that you thought, but uh, you know, certainly it's it's great to be able to have that taken care of. just a few days, but have you learned anything about what Tai Simpson's bringing to to the table? >> No, we haven't we haven't been able to do enough yet to be able to get that, you know, and that's really for the rookies just in general. I mean, we're so limited. You're doing jog throughs had a little bit of seven on seven, which it's a necessary thing. I think it's the most unrealistic drill that there exists in football. Um, you know, because these rushes are real and uh and you don't feel that. And so, he's done a really good job like the rest of the class has of just coming in, learning, getting to know his teammates. you know, Dave Veron does such a great job with those quarterbacks as a whole, whether that's Matthew, Tai, S, you know, um, Stson, um, you know, so it's been it's been really good. >> Coach, when you look at CJ Daniels and where he came from out of Coach Crystal Ball's, you know, system and now he's coming into yours, but also being in that room with Devonte and Puka, what do you envision for him? Obviously bringing him along and as he gets activated, >> I think just that, Nick, you know, and he's u he's got a maturity. He's got a good look in his eye. um you know, you feel his presence even just in the meeting room and his engagement to be able to answer questions. Um you know, but again, it's really early on any of these rookies, but liked his body of work. Uh like the background that we did from people that you really trust and value their opinions, but I mean, you're talking about Devonte, you're talking about Puka, um you know, Jordan Whittington, Mumfield's looked really good, Xavier Smith obviously played a bunch of meaningful snaps for us. And so and then we got some guys on the practice squad that you know you know look more comfortable going into their second year hearing some of these plays and these concepts but um been pleased but again it's still so early for us to say I'll be able to have a little bit better feel once we put the pads on in camp and things like that. >> What is he done to help Cuka at all? If anything he's back here now with the stuff he's been dealing with in the offseason. >> I think he just you know listen to understand communicate to connect. you know, you guys know how much love I have for our players in general, but you know, you know, I've always talked about just his heart and I I think um you know, he talked to you guys. I think we can all feel the authenticity and you know, I think I know that uh when I was younger and and still now, you know, you give people grace and you try to understand every single thing and how can you be there to help, you know, them continue to just, you know, move in the direction that they want and that those things are never- ending journeys. you're always becoming and um I love his security and being able to be, you know, authentically honest about it. I think there's real strength in some of the vulnerabilities and I'm I'm really proud of him and and proud of a lot of guys, but I'm really proud of Puka. >> Have you seen a change in him? >> I just think you just that light shines just a little bit brighter, you know? He's just got this he's got this light about him in general that always kind of shines, but it seems like it's shining about as bright as this light in my eye right now. Um, but he's he's been great, you know, and and um, you know, I've always appreciated his ability to kind of let me in and um, it's uh, it's really cool to be able to just see the kind of the direction that he's on and we'll have our arm around him and continue to support him throughout. >> What's it been like having Brian Allen, Rod Woods out there on the field? >> It's been great. You know, it's funny when you go through it, you realize that we've been here for a little bit when we got former players circling back, but I think, you know, you talk about guys that were foundational pieces. Everybody throws the word culture around. The culture is the people and people like Robert Woods and Brian Allen, the toughness mentally and physically, their play style, their ability to be able to communicate how important it was to them, their consistent authenticity and who they were where I think that bred a, you know, that led to a trust that they had from their teammates and from their coaches. And they both work really hard and they love football and they love, you know, they love coaching and connecting and helping elevate people. And that's what coaching is really about. And um I'm really grateful that when they decided to step into this arena, they wanted to be here because they had options to go elsewhere as >> What's the process been like in terms of um trying to figure out how these all these pieces in the secondary fit together during OTAAS? >> You know, it's been a good positive one. You know, Jimmy Lake, Coach Beak, um Mike Hunter, Coach Schula, you know, they've done a really good job of, you know, guys are learning really all all the spots on the back end. No different than really Ryan Wendell cross trains, you know, our guys from the inside to outside. Um, but you know, you're seeing Trent McDuffy all over. There's certain guys that'll play just safety or just play outside corner, but then you got a lot of guys that can play safety, they can play the star position, they can play dime money. Um, but we're teaching concepts, Adam. And so, um, that flexibility and that understanding of what are the core coverage contours that we want to play, what does that look like out of three down, out of four down front mechanics, out of some of the known rush packages. But um I've really been pleased with the trajectory of the teaching progression and then the guys ability to be able to give the feedback showed in some of these jogthroughs and then we've done some seven on where you know it that's a really you know that's tilted towards the offense and I think we've had some really good competitive plays defensively that I've been really proud of those guys and I I just like the competitiveness and I like the connection of the group that you can feel. >> Did Matthew come Did Matthew come to you for advice when he was coaching the girls? No, he's uh he's I don't think he needs much advice. You know, he he's uh he's been doing that with those girls for a while, but I've you know, Kelly sent me that video and I said, "What am I supposed to do now? You can take my job as well." You know, I don't really have much place, you know, here. So, I did see that though very he's much more patient than I am. >> Talked about you told him to be a good communicator. You talked about it was difficult for him to ask for help for you. Can you talk about the balance of X's and O's Shawn McVey versus helping a young man off the field? >> Yeah, I think um you know, and I've been open with it and we've talked about this previously. I think the most important thing is is when you're reminded of why you do this, it's it's to shine a light on others and and you know, it's such a blessing to do this job. And don't get me wrong, we're competitive. You love the mastery of what this game entails and helping guys improve. But um you know, Coach Wooden used to say, you know, if you want to see people's jump shots improved, let's coach their hearts and I bet the jump shot will improve in the meantime. And so we want to be transformational. And I think that's way more important. Who are we becoming as a result of what we're doing while also trying to be great football players and a great team. And I think better people make better Rams. Um and you know, and there's there's carryover into personally and professionally. And so I think um you know, my heart's changed from a lot of the experiences. It's never ending of trying to be better, but you know, having my wife Veronica, having those two boys, being around people that I'm inspired to want to do better for them, whether that's our coaches, our players, our ownership group, you know, leading alongside Les and Tony and Kevin, you know, so I feel really grateful to have players like Puka and really just the people that I'm around in general, um, that make you want to be better with the right purpose and the right perspective, and that's what it's about. You mentioned before on the podcast about, you know, at one point you thought about, you know, quitting at some point, but you had your wife and everybody around you. How much those do those experiences are where you're able to relate to the players that do go through things mentally and emotionally to be able to guide them? >> A lot. you know, I don't think I was ever secure enough to really acknowledge my shortcomings or some of those flaws because um you know, you're really you're probably not secure enough to really be vulnerable and to be honest about where you were, but when you look back on it, I think the best thing that occurred was some of that adversity. You don't want to go through it again, but if you can really understand like the stuff that you say, but then do you really believe setbacks or setups for comebacks? Do you really believe growth demands discomfort? and having had tangible experiences where you don't grow through it unless you actually go through it. And so, um, but you do realize you're never alone, you know. And I think that's where my wife, so many people in this organization are people that love you unconditionally are able to tell you what you need to hear, not necessarily what you want to hear. Um, and so those are things that I think are honest and you know, and that's part of my journey. Uh, but I'm better for having gone through that, but that doesn't mean that I still don't have to work really hard to continue to develop skills to be the person that you want to be. And I tell guys all the time, I don't expect perfection, but what are those things that guide your perspective that serve as your, you know, your compass, if you will. Um, and usually when you follow those things, you never regret it. But it's a lot easier to say than to do. And, uh, you know, we want to be about it on, uh, you know, on a daily basis as much as we can. Sean, I know you said seven on seven pretty unrealistic, but you and Matthew seemed pretty excitable. There were a few plays out there. Like, what do you think that was indicative of? >> Well, what do you think it was indicative of? I I was excited when there's good football in general, Lindsay. But, um, I think Matthew would be the first to tell you too going into year 18 that uh if we could play seven on seven, you know, we probably would have never had any of those back issues that we've had. You know, those those rushes are very real. Um, but that's not real football, you know. But I do think it's necessary for teaching coverage is route distribution, but there's not like if you were to say one of the most important things for a quarterback, it's feeling a real rush and what does that look like and playing within the timing and rhythm, but this is uh what we can do in the uh settings in uh in OTAAS, which it's hard to stomach as a coach, but hey, we'll follow it. when you when you guys are all rooted like this this time of year, what what does development look like for a young quarterback like Tai? What do you hope that he gets out of this? >> Yeah, I think really just, you know, setting foundations. You know, we've really talked about this, Nate, the offseason's about setting foundations and the fundamentals because you can work those things and, you know, hey, what does it look like to be able to communicate, especially as a quarterback, how am I saying the plays? You know, I would expect him, you know, as Dave's going through stuff, like you got to see plays when you're saying them. Otherwise, you can't call plays in this offense. And so you got to be able to see them when you say them. Practicing in the mirror. What does your voice inflection look like? How are you emphasizing certain things? How are you really being able to go through the mechanics of everything that happens before the snap? And then what's my footwork? What's my timing and rhythm? And so just getting a feel for some of those things that you can do in routes on air in seven on the overall operation and some of the jogthroughs. But there's nothing like playing 11 on 111. And uh I do think that what you know the pros that I've been around that operate at a really high level, they know how to be able to practice at full speed while minimizing the risk for injury um when we don't take guys to the ground. Those those settings are more uh applicable once we do get into training camp where you're actually playing with pads on. Um but we'll make the most of it. So it's really setting foundations and just getting the fundamentals and and some of the stuff that you can control above the neck. >> Okay. Thanks guys. See you guys.

title: Texans All Access | What Stood Out at the First OTA Practice
text: Hello Texans. It's OTAA time. Mark and John with you to review our first OTAA session. The team's been at it for a while. It's phase three. One OTAA practice before we saw the practice that we just witnessed, Johnny. And they've been at it for weeks doing various activities, but now we've got some 11 on 111, 7 on seven. And it's important to point out that this is not the only thing that they're doing. So you hear stuff in the media, you hear some reviews, reactions. They're out there a lot more often than what the media sees. I think that's very important to point out. >> Yeah, absolutely. With all the different position groups where there are or might be some position battles. Again, OTAAS are voluntary. So, not everybody is on site. It's giving other guys opportunities to step into a role, step in with the twos or the ones or whatever it might be during practice. So, it's a good it's a good opportunity for a lot of people to show what they can do. Not the full squad, but enough that you just get really excited about what this team can do in 26. Well, we're all excited about the offensive line because they had so many additions and you saw a lot of different combinations in this OTAA practice because some of the periods are more like choreography, individual drills and then you have the 11 on 111 and not everybody's going to do everything. You can't tell much until you put pads on when it comes from a O line Dline perspective, but we've taken strides tremendously when it comes to the communication up on up front. So, I'm I'm proud of what I seen so far and I'm excited to see where it's going to go for us. How important is tight end play in this offense?
