He's done a great job of just, you know, he's just a football guy. You talk about a guy who knows how to have fun at practice, lighten up. You talk about a guy who brings joy to the room, you know, that's Foster. He's done a great job of working with Marlin as well. And adding Marlin, getting Brevin back. Got some young guys who are truly young at their at their position and still have a lot of room to grow. So, I'm excited about the the growth potential of the room from the tight end position. >> Coach, I know it's just first day of TA's t-shirt, shorts, no hats, no tack, but there was a lot of competitive juices flowing out there. as a coach when you're back when you're standing back looking at that. How impressed are you by the fact that these guys are ready to get after? >> For us being day two and from where I stand, it's uh it's very impressive to see just the back and forth nature of our team to see guys barking at each other, see the competitive the competitiveness of our team. And I I told our team in in our team meetings like I know everybody in our room is competitive. Like you wouldn't be here if you're not a competitor. So, we have the com a great competitive spirit, great competitive fire on all sides of the ball, all three phases. And that's what that's what it takes to build a really good team. You got to come out here and you got to compete in a smart control manner in OTAAS, but you can still compete and that's what the guys are doing today. A lot of back and forth, not just one side dominating the other side, but a lot of competitive plays going on and that makes me proud as a coach. though, you got uh late session there where Will Anderson Jr. really gets after the offense. There was a four or five play stretch where he kind of wrecked the whole deal. What have you seen from him this off season? How how how does he kind of raise the level out there when he gets after it like that? >> Yeah, Will continues to wreck practice. I'm probably going to have to sit him out here soon cuz we have to be able to actually practice. So, he just keeps wrecking practice. So, that's just keep doing that. Keep causing havoc. That's what he does. And I was showing guys that's what he does on Sundays as well. So it's no surprise with Will is the the guy for everyone to watch of the intensity at which we operate. That's how Will Anderson plays. That's how I want everybody to be. >> Is it possible real quick that that he that he can take this thing to like a different level already pro? Is it possible there's more? >> There is definitely more for Will uh on the field. He's always, you know, fine-tuning his craft. He's working extra as always with Rod and with Frank before practice, working on the the small intricacies of hand placement and those things as a pass rusher. But where I've seen him take another step this year is just his leadership of being vocal, right, as a leader for our team. Like being that guy, you know, he'll he has no issue bringing the team up, letting everybody know, hey, this wasn't a good day. Let's pick it up. or he does a great job as well of encouraging guys when he sees it done the right way. So, him taking that step as a vocal leader is where I've seen his growth already happen this year. >> Uh, how you, your staff and your players, how you able to cope with everything that is going inside the stadium with all the sort of world being so close? >> With the World Cup being here, I would say the World Cup has done a great job of working with us. Um, and they've I know it's going to be an awesome event here in Houston of the World Cup and uh, you know, everybody can't wait for it to to happen, but they've been gracious. They've been working well with us, and I'm I'm thankful for their partnership and how they work with us through this transition. There's a lot going on here around the stadium. A lot of spaces and things have to be moved around, but they've been outstanding to work with. Right. Hey, what's been your I know it's still early, but what's been your impression of the young guys and how they're working in and and adapting to everything? >> I feel like all of our young guys are are really up to speed and what we've been able to do. Our coaches are doing a great job of taking advantage of the additional time that we have with the rookies to teach them what we do, how we do it, and the rookies have picked it up really well. We got a really smart group of rookies who stepped in and at times you don't even know they're rookies because they're not making the normal rookie mistakes. They're fitting in just fine. It's always some technique and small things to clean up, but they're they're fitting into what we do, especially culturally. Like, we got the right guys with the mindset. We got the right guys. They're going to be physical. They're smart. They're tough guys. So, it's just a matter of them continuing to get reps. And the more reps they get, the better they'll get this year. How do you how do you feel about the thrills of both Jaden Higgins and Jaylen Nola's office going too? >> Yeah, for when I look at these guys in the offseason our receiver position I really Higgins has done a really great job of taking advantage of the offseason really coming back in shape. He's looking bigger, stronger, faster, which is what you expect for a secondyear player of his caliber. is definitely, you know, taking advantage of it and I I'm looking I'm really excited to see what it's going to look like this season. Know he's going to have a really good year based on how he looks right now. He's in shape. He's ready to roll. Jay No is doing a really great job as well improving at his craft and uh how we're able to move him around different areas doing a great job, you know, as a as a kick returner and we're punt returner. We're emphasizing him, you know, working on getting vertical. He's doing a really great job of working on those things as well. So, both guys are taking the necessary steps to improve. >> At this point in your coaching career where it it feels like you're kind of to the point where you can mentor guys more under you. Uh the news that Jordan Hicks, who you mentored as a player, what's it like for you to kind of go from when I was a vet, kind of took me under my wing to now he might get into coaching and he's going under your wing. Do you feel kind of like more of a veteran coach now? >> Uh for having Jordan in with our, you know, Bill Walsh diversity fellowship program. Um, man, I'm fired up to have him in. I know just from being around him as a player, I know he's capable, very capable of coaching or doing whatever he wants to do. But I just wanted Jordan to come in and just get a taste of coaching and see how he how he would like it. And he's already done a great job. I I see coaching his future. He's always been a very smart player, a guy knew when I saw Jordan when we drafted Jordan there in Philly and first day he suited up and started doing drills, he looks way better than me. So, I'm probably out of here. So, I'm uh I'm happy to be able to, you know, have a guy in who's played a long career and he's taken the little that I was able to do in mentoring him, teaching him about some leadership. He's taken that to the new heights. He's helped a lot of guys there in Philly, also in Arizona, Cleveland, everywhere he's been. He's been a standup guy. Tremendous young man, great family man. So, I'm happy to be able to have him. Happy to also had former teammate Darren Sprouls who's here with us uh for the program. You know, you talk about a outstanding player, but so humble, right? 15-year career guy who's done it at the highest level. I could never cover this guy ever in practice. He's a outstanding talent, but he's here working with our running backs, our returners, and he's already had an impact on those guys. >> Uh seeing Breon Jordan back on the field, could it mean for you guys? Have you had any special conversations with him? Is he on a pitch count at all? And then also and then update on Tang when he might be able to practice. >> Brevin's out. He's rolling. Doing a great job. Back to where he's been. Always here. Big smile on his face. Excited to practice. You know, we're we're easing him back in. He had a a really big play yesterday on a choice route. He man got to the proper depth. Broke one of our safeties off and had a really nice play. So, I mean, it was exciting, right, to see him just back on the field. But we know how devastating it was for him to go down and to see him back working is very encouraging. I'm proud of the work that he's put in. Tank is still working off on the side. When that time is, you know, set for him to be back, he'll be back out there. >> You tell us what you like about Marte Mu. >> Yeah, Marte. What I like about him, he's a very smart linebacker. Smart. He's he's long, fast guy, but Marte does a really good job of being where he's supposed to be in position. and he's communicating. We're moving him around. He's taking some reps at the mic linebacker spot, so he does a really good job of communicating. And he's also taking some spots at the at the some reps at the wheel linebacker. So, smart guy who you're able to move around at multiple spots. He's done a really good job on special teams as well. So, just a very versatile, athletic linebacker. Still a young player. Young player who's I think he's played in three or four different schemes already to be so young in his career. So hoping he just settles settles in. So what we're being able to teach him. Coach Billy Davis done an outstanding job of working with him this off season. Marte type of guy. He's always in the building. We have to kick him out. So he's always doing the extras, the film, the recovery, body maintenance. He's a he's a true worker. So I'm proud to see how how he transitions and how he looks during training camp. for a few more years. Speaking of unfortunately, injury to EJ Speed creates some competition there too for some of these other guys who are already competing for spots and for their niche. Uh just what do you how do you see it and what tough loss is that to have EJ go down? >> The competition is high at every position. Uh we unfortunately we won't have EJ for some time, but we'll see how that recovery process goes. I'm hopeful that we'll get EJ back at some point And then uh I mean you're going to be pretty busy the next couple of weeks. What happen you plan on going to any of the games you're particular? >> I have not planned on the world going to any World Cup games at this time. Got a few family vacations playing. So excited excited about that. But uh I know it'll be man outstanding time. If I get the opportunity to go to a match I definitely would like to. >> Hey coach right here. This is uh year four for you and uh as head coach. Uh I'm really curious to hear how your process has changed and evolved from coming in at 2023 now coming into 2026 in the summer. How you've changed is also how you've seen the process change for guys like CJ Henry and other guys that kind of came in that class with you. >> Yeah. The unique thing about being year four I look at every year I just start over, right? So I start over. I always analyze everything from the standpoint of, hey, why are we doing what we're doing from a practice schedule standpoint, from rep count, like what are we doing? So, I always just look at it with a fresh set of eyes, not just kind of rinse and repeat. Just because we did something in 2023 doesn't mean that we're doing that right now. Our team has definitely changed a lot. Coaching staff has changed. So, as a coach, I think you're I'm always growing and evolving because that's what the game does. The game evolves. I'm constantly looking at different schemes, different looking at different things we can add and tweak to our offense, to our defense to make us as successful as possible. >> Anything you wish you did sooner or wish that you didn't do maybe earlier on? >> For me, I think everything is I couldn't have asked for a better, you know, three-year start. So everything is going, you know, way better than I could have ever hoped for. So I'm I'm thankful. I'm blessed with the people that I get to work with. It's just uh I'm blessed thankful for this opportunity and looking to continue to grow it to make Houston a very special place, which it is already, but we're trying to do something very special here and we got the people to do that. >> I'll take those last two. you you briefly touched on it like having to evolve your scheme. I'm sure team offense is really going to be studying you all since you all had so much success last year, you know, as a as a defensive play caller and defensive mind. How do you prepare against that when you know teams are trying to figure out how to stop? >> Yeah, for me it's it's no different this year just because we had success last year. Every year offenses are going to study, right, the top defensive in the league. And we've we've been that for past however many years we've been a top defense. So a lot of offenses are going to study us. They're going to try different schemes, different type of plays to try to beat our defense. But for me, I'm looking at the same thing as well. So schematically, I don't believe you ever just stay the same. You have to tweak, you have to adjust, you have to adapt your scheme because, you know, offenses are doing the same thing. So, we're not we're not just sitting back and resting on what we did last year. I don't believe in that. Last year is over. We got a lot of new guys here who have to c get up to speed with what we're doing, but we have to kind of fit and tailor our scheme to what those guys do best, and that's what we'll do this year. >> Last one, DJ. turn it off. >> How have you just kind of seen the other receivers outside of Pico develop throughout this off season to try to compliment what he also brings as an >> every every player is different. So I don't look at the position as someone needs to compliment Nico. My message to our guys is how are you executing exactly what our coaches are asking you to do. So it's never about complimenting one guy or another. Let's execute the right way. Let's coach it up the right way. And everybody, if you excel the proper way, if we're running the offense right in the manner, which we should, and our quarterback can go through, progress, whoever is open should get the football. But you got to be doing the right thing. Even if you're on the back side of a concept, are you doing those things that you're supposed to do? >> Thank you, coach. >> All right. Thank you, Go.

text: the mic. >> Good afternoon. >> When you look at the overall practice, having everybody all together, rookies, vets, what are you thinking of the team so far at this stage of the offseason? What have you seen from him this off season? How how how does he kind of raise the level out there when he gets after it like that? >> Yeah, Will continues to wreck practice. I'm probably going to have to sit him out here soon because we have to be able to actually practice. So, he just keeps wrecking practice. So, that's just keep doing that. Keep causing havoc. That's what he does. And I was showing guys that's what he does on Sundays as well. So it's no surprise with Will is the the guy for everyone to watch of the intensity at which we operate. That's how Will Anderson plays. That's how I want everybody to be. >> Is it possible real quick that that he that he can take this thing to like a different level already pro? Is it possible there's more? >> There is definitely more for Will uh on the field. He's always, you know, fine-tuning his craft. He's working extra as always with Rod and with Frank before practice. Working on the the small intricacies of hand placement and those things as a pass rusher. But where I've seen him take another step this year is just his leadership of being vocal, right? So, him taking that step as a vocal leader is where I've seen his growth already happen this year. >> Uh, how you, your staff and your players, how you able to cope with everything at any point inside the stadium with all the World Cup being so close? >> With the World Cup being here, I would say the World Cup has done a great job of working with us. We're really trying to get the foundation and u some of the team components we'll kind of build as we go during the offseason as far as the the team uh periods and just kind of the tempo in which those are practiced. >> Does does all the speed you added beyond the obvious? Does that help with like the timing and the spacing and some of the stuff you guys want to be able to do what happens? >> Speed like the receiver room and whatnot. >> Tight ends, receivers, running backs. It just seems like speed like >> Yeah, no doubt. Speed's a weapon and uh speed allows you to uh threaten the defense in multiple ways and uh you know certainly I think I think just the size and the speed combination of some of our skill positions obviously is really valuable. I think for our receivers there's speed but there's also size. I think uh you know that goes into the run game. You know receivers have to block in this league for you to run the football really really well. And um you know I think you watch when we line up there there's some size there that I think is going to be beneficial for us in the run game. you know, some guys that can we're going to be asked to do some dirty work at times and then off of that create some great opportunities in the pass game if we can provide that opportunity to assist in the run game. >> What about the like the tight ends? Like they all seem like four four guys like what what is it what does that do? >> Yeah, they all got size, they all got juice, they can separate and and make some plays downfield which will be obviously beneficial for us and uh you know when you're with you know have a couple tight ends on the field uh you don't want to limit your your threat downfield. >> I was specifying on Jordan Tyson. Yeah. >> Did he do any field work yesterday? >> He was out there doing a little bit. Yeah. Just a little bit. >> Will he incorporate with like I don't know seven on sevens or full offense? >> Uh he won't do any seven on seven today. Um he'll do a couple of the more the walkthrough type speeds. >> And what what's your philosophy in I mean do you like all rookies? You're a rookie you have to start with the second or third team or or if someone like him or a higher draft pick shows that they're ready right away. They can get first team reps as early as >> Yeah. It's case by case I think. Um, we put Kelvin at left tackle last year. I mean, we weren't going to fool anyone with that one. So, uh, put him at left tackle, give him as many reps with those guys as we can. Uh, you know, Jordan will quickly start working with those top guys as we go. And so, uh, yeah, and other guys will have opportunities to kind of work their way up quickly. So, >> what do you say to Julian Black? >> Julian is a big- time leader. Uh, super smart. Uh, you know, when you put him and Justin Reed on and back there and you got Yonas back there with those guys, uh, that's really high football IQ and those guys can work hand in hand together really, really well. Just I think the fun part is if you go out there and watch them in practice, just watch them talk and communicate and all the non-verbals that they do. Uh, I think it's really really high level. >> Some guys for like that that slot corner role and is is he one of them? I think really almost just about our whole safety room has the ability to go there and then we have some corners and so u you'll see some of those guys there. U we'll continue to rotate that as the whole offseason goes and um you know I think the versatility and the flexibility of our back end is really key. I think sometimes you get stuck in corners and safeties and it's like it's DBs, you know, they got to they all got to have some cover components and uh in the way we play we got to be able have some versatility there. So, it's like a open audition kind of right now like just kind of >> Yeah, I think you'll see Jonas there obviously uh you know you'll see some of those other safeties there as we go. Certainly, we have some corners who've played you know predominantly star position as as they've played in their career and so it'll be a rotation. >> How much of a leap do you think Tyler can make in his second season? >> Yeah, leaps. Um, I don't know how to quantify leaps, but I I do know he's got a great opportunity to kind of just continue to build and uh, you know, when you have a full off season with your core group, your starting group, um, all the communication, all the continuity that that creates is really powerful because, uh, you know, there's different tools that he can utilize, the more comfortable he gets as far as, you know, getting in and out of things and having the command and control of the thing. And so, um, yeah, I think it's been great this whole offseason so far. And because you guys like run so many sevens this time of year, like is how do you measure kind of his progress? Like are you looking I think like the Cleveland Brown like Tom Lincoln was like if the ball hits the ground that's like fairly like do you kind of have a similar philosophy like how do you kind of value >> I we'll we'll break it down statistically. I mean we're still going to use the stats to you know tie it all together but you know this is part of this process is u you know you're evaluating decision-m you're evaluating the actual physical components of it. Um, you know, and you got to test yourself in these these spaces. Again, uh, I think that's an important part for these quarterbacks is you got to test yourself. You got to, you know, test the boundaries of things and and see what you can and can't do. >> What is, uh, Martin Emerson's participation level at this phase of the offseason and and what is your projection for him? He'll he'll work mostly at outside corner and he's in that slot. >> So, mostly outside corner. Um, his most exposure in the league has been out there. Um, I mean, he's he's impressive, you know, looking at him, you know, size, strength. Uh, you know, he's got some speed. He can play on the red line. Those are hard downs, and I think he's done it in this league for a number of years. Um, you know, again, similar guy. He's coming off of an injury like a lot of guys, and so you're always going to be conscious of that as we kind of build him as we go. But, uh, you know, he's had a great first exposure. >> You signed Jackson. Can you talk about it? Yeah, we only had five linebackers and so uh we knew at some point we'd have to hopefully acquire another one and so uh we had a workout the other day with you know about five or six participants in there and Jackson did an excellent job. um you know he's been with the Jets for a couple years on their practice squad participating with them been up a few times and so he's got great exposure uh in this league and so uh you know if anything you know the the father-son thing was maybe a little bit of a you know can be a little bit of a contrary uh thing for him but uh they've worked together at Cal before which I think is really beneficial that uh Pete and Jackson worked together and so that's nothing new and uh it'll be great. >> Um Kendrick Miller has come back from a knee injury. what is his stat? >> Yeah, still working through the recovery process and so um you know won't necessarily see him out there in the in the football elements but um he's done an awesome job. Are there any other um guys injured from last season who won't be participating from the football like Deon Wheel or >> um >> No, I mean there's there's some guys again we'll limit a lot of these guys um as we go. But uh you know this is a back first of a backtoback so you kind of got to make sure these guys recover and some guys will kind of slow down a little bit today and you know every week we'll just kind of look at it from an evaluation standpoint. You mentioned uh Pete's role as far as a leadership standpoint, but any expectations for him like his play, his field? >> Pete Warner. >> Pete Warner thought Pete played really good football last year. Uh I think he's he's a really clean player. He plays really sound football and uh you know when you put him and Kaden and you know Stzman and a bunch of those guys like they've played together and they have some continuity and so um I think that's a really good group for us. What are you expecting out of Danny in year two? Danny starts >> Danny um I think just continue to build. I think we saw him as the season went on. He was able to earn more and more reps and opportunities that had more to do with him than anything else. He was a really good player and so um you know we're expecting that you know I think there's always this rookie year to second year jump that a lot of these guys make just because it's their first full calendar now of the NFL. They can kind of use the whole offseason. They're not into the whole 40 yard dash, you know, training program that you have to kind of navigate before your rookie year. And so it's a really great opportunity just to grow. >> By the time camp, regular season, whatever might be rolls on, do you ideally hope that there's one guy defined in that star role or do you see more value in that being? >> N there's going to have to be someone who kind of takes the predominant role. Uh but again, position, versatility, and flexibility is important. You're going have to have multiple guys play there. that most of the off season when we've asked you or Mickey about Alvin Camra, it's mostly been we're figuring out the roster and yeah, >> things are kind of fluid at some point maybe soon. Do you have kind of a date when you'd like to say this is done so you know it's either finite or it's in the past? >> Yeah, I I don't think we you put timelines on any of this stuff. Um, you know, we're just kind of working through the roster and again this time of year there's, you know, some of these guys they traditionally haven't come this time of year, which is, you know, is part of their kind of rhythm and routine as far as, uh, the offseason program and so, uh, we'll just work continue to work through that. >> I know it is early, but have you seen a difference in Tyler just even the last months or out on the field? Like just >> I think it's just continue to build, continue to stack. I thought I finished the season off really well, played really good football. um you get a full off season and so um I think he's in an excellent spot. >> You feel like it's changed for him or maybe he's responded to the fact that there's not you know we've talked about it before with no quarterback competition and all those other things, but like just what have you seen from him over the course of the past few weeks fitting into that role most immediately? >> I think there's a leadership component when you know you know you're kind of leading the charge. there's a there's a leadership thing that he's certainly uh showcased throughout this whole offseason just with you know kind of rallying these guys and working as much as they have worked through this whole offseason and then uh from an onfield standpoint obviously he's got a great foundation with what we you know did last year we're going to make plenty of adjustments and had little nuances and he's a part of that process and so I think that's the fun part of this is every day we're going to kind of be able to build off of something we've done in the past we're going to be able to put some new stuff in and make some adjustments and uh build it together. >> Eric had shared a story. Eric McCoy had shared a story about um something didn't go exactly to plan on a practice rep and Tyler was the guy that kind of led the charge of rehuddling and and doing it again. >> Um how often do you see that kind of approach from him on the detail orientation and and just from your perspective, why is that important? >> I think it's an excellent example of um at the end day these guys are going to make the plays. These guys are going to lead the charge. Um our job is to guide them and lead them in our capacity. Um, you know, Tyler's done an excellent job with that leadership role. Um, you know, we got to get it right, we got to, uh, play really clean football and so, um, when it's not right, our guys have the urgency to get it right. >> How are you approaching this particular offseason activities portion? Last year was, you know, the first year coaching staff, but this year more established, you had a lot of roster turnover >> as far as >> just how you approach it, how different it is for you. >> I think for us, obviously, there's some continuity. There's always going to be change. That's what the NFL is. And so you're always on boarding new players and uh new personnel and coaches and you just want to get everyone on the same page with the same uh philosophical approach. Uh that's going to happen. Um other than that, you know, obviously we've found a rhythm and routine based off of last year and we'll adjust that all the time, but I think our guys are doing really well right now. >> Have you guys set up joint practices at all for training camp? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. So again, kind of mentioned to you guys, our goal is to, you know, get that going a little bit more and so I feel great about it. But I feel like our goal during training camp, we'll be in Medie similar to last year for the primary focus of our camp, which is great because we get to stay in the community. Jackson will be here. We'll uh do a joint practice with Jacksonville uh right here in Medie. And then uh when we go out to California for the Rams, we'll do a joint practice with Dallas and LA separately uh while we're out there. So I think uh you know these joint practices I believe in them just my exposure to them as a as a coach and u it gives you a chance to get really good work with particularly your starters and your number ones and uh you know I think a lot of it comes down to teaming up with the right you know other organizations and I feel like we got that this year. >> So you guys will stay out in California after that game >> we'll do them all before that game >> before the Rams game. >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. We'll do Dallas, LA, and then play them in preseason. >> Let's before you get started, we'll take like two or three. >> No, I was just follow Dallas and Dallas and Oxnard, is that right? >> Yeah, they'll be out in Oxnard and then Rams will do out there as well. >> Question, what impressions of Jamal? >> Awesome. Fired up. Uh I didn't know him personally in any way. U obviously follow him. He was in Dallas when I was there and um obviously followed the magic the last few years and what they've kind of been able to build there and so uh I think it's awesome for us. It's awesome for us. I'm fired up for him and uh I'm excited to kind of be able to overlap a little bit more uh as we go as you know he's got a lot of stuff going on right now but you know hopefully he comes over here a little bit. I'll probably bother him over there just to you know see their experience and kind of get to know uh their approach to things and you can always learn from these guys. >> Thanks. >> All right. Thanks.

title: Geno Smith and Garrett Wilson on the Start of OTAs | New York Jets | NFL
text: Good afternoon. >> Just a question. >> You look You look familiar. >> How you doing, Gary? Good to see you. >> Yes. Good to see you guys. >> Welcome back. >> Thank you. Thank you. >> Gina, was there a time, you know, where you came here and it was just kind of surreal? And has that, you know, did you have that feeling when you first got back here? >> Yeah, I would say my first day back in the building. Um, you know, just the f, you know, coming in for physicals and, uh, just walking down that hall again, you know, was the f very first hall I walked down when I, you know, got drafted and, uh, you know, all those feelings come back, just great feelings, great memories, you know, seeing my mom in the locker room and, you know, I started just thinking about, you know, just my first time in the NFL, first time here. But, uh, immediately it clicked right back in. I got to get to work and, uh, you know, I just, you know, got right back to that. And so, I'm really excited to be here. and, you know, even seeing, you know, all you guys' faces again, you know, it's really cool. >> What's it been like learning Frank's offense and how would you describe it? >> You know, it's been uh, you know, first of all, you know, Coach Reichs has done a a phenomenal job with teaching. Um, he's very detailed in the way that he teaches the offense, very meticulous in in what he wants and uh, from us and how he wants us to execute. Um, it's been it's been great. Um, you know, to answer your question, I think we're building one day at a time. Um, we're competing. We're getting better. uh every single day and Coach Reich is is leading that ship and uh you know with him at the helm man I feel really great about it. >> What's the what's the process been like for you getting in sync with Garrett because he's obvious such a unique player and he has the ability to he can improvise on his shots and stuff. >> Yeah. Uh it's really you know Garrett's a great player and uh he makes me better man. Like they make it, you know, those guys out there make it really really simple for me. I just got to read the defense and throw it to, you know, whoever the defense tells me to throw it to because they're all really good and there's only one football, you know, that's the bad part about I wish I could throw it to all of them, you know, but it's only one football and uh, you know, Garrett's a great player and, you know, my job is to to help bring out the best in him and vice versa. Um, and that goes for all of my teammates and so, you know, really I just want to continue to build build on our chemistry. Uh, we're working extremely hard on the field and every single day I can see the progress and so that's a good sign. Uh but obviously we're a long ways away and we got a lot of work to do. >> We talked uh Bruce Hall. He talked about how y'all working out together and like that. How's it been getting to know him and everything? >> Yeah, it's cool, man. Like he was training in Florida um down in Miami and you know with one of my old trainers and you know I was training somewhere else and I just kind of you know left that alone. I went to where Breeze was at uh the minute I knew I was going to be here. Uh it was extremely important for me to get to know him off the field, you know, and that goes for all of my teammates as well, to get to know these guys off the field so we can develop that bond and that trust where when we step on the field, we all understand that we're playing for one another and uh you know, Bree is a great guy. Um, you know, I got that feeling from him the first, you know, moment I met him. Um, but he's also a great player and so again, I want to try and bring out the best in him and I know he's going to push me as well. You know, obviously it's so early, but what are your biggest takeaways from these first two days about what this team is capable of? >> Man, I see a lot of potential. You know, I see a lot of potential in this team. I think, uh, AG is doing a great job at, you know, showing us the vision of what he wants for the team and how he wants us to go out there and play and be Jets. And, uh, you know, for me as the quarterback of the team, I know that there's a lot of work to be put in. And so I really focus on that is, you know, try to focus on the day-to-day just getting better, leading the guys, um, bringing that energy, that juice to the practice field so that we can all, you know, go out there and execute the plays we need to, and then, you know, as the days go by, you know, just continuing to get better and continue to compete. I mean, that's really all it's about. >> From your first, you know, the history of this franchise and obviously how much have you thought about being the guy now to finally end that playoff uh, stroke? Yeah, I mean those things are so far ahead of us, you know. Um me being in the league as long as I've been, I understand that you can only focus on what's right in front of you and that's being in the moment, staying in the moment. Um we want to be the best team in the world. You know, I don't I don't feel shy about saying that. But I understand that there's a lot of work, like I said, to be done, and you got to focus on the work. You focus on getting better every single day. And then you focus on your performance on, you know, on Sundays or whenever the day comes. Um and it's a collective thing. you know, we all got to make up our minds and say this is what we're going to be. And I can see that building, you know, but it's still, you know, so so early in the process. >> You know, how are you a different quarterback and a different person from the first time you were here? >> I've just gotten older, you know, a lot more experienced. Um, you know, overall, you know, I've always felt like I've had talent, but I feel like my fundamentals have grown. Um, and that's on and off the field. I feel like the leadership aspect has grown uh throughout my experience in the league and all the great quarterbacks that I've been around, great coordinators, uh as well as just, you know, I'm I'm a lot more calm. You know, it's a lot more a lot less of what am I, you know, trying to figure out what to expect. Uh I kind of know what to expect now. And so, uh just, you know, just a lot more calm in my demeanor. You you guys might notice that. But, uh overall, you know, still the same guy. Still got the same passion for the game. um still study as as hard as I did when I was you know a rookie trying to figure out the NFL and uh for me it's just about getting better every day and that's where you know I f put my focus. >> Did you feel pressure the first time because you were such a high draft choice here? >> I I put a lot of pressure on myself you know and uh you know the pressure for me was to go out there and you know try and make something of my NFL career and I think that goes for everybody who gets drafted into the NFL or who gets a chance in the NFL. Um, you know, the key thing for me back then was, you know, put the time in, put the work in, you know, figure out the unknowns. You know, there's a lot of unknowns for a rookie. Um, now that I've, you know, played in the league for, you know, a number of years, there's a lot less unknowns. And so, uh, it just allows me to process things a little bit faster, but you're still learning. You know, anybody would tell you that there's always going to be a lot of learning going on, uh, you know, in the NFL because it's, you know, it's the best of the best and you got to get better. >> So, you don't feel that type of pressure anymore? Honestly, I, you know, without, you know, I don't want to, you know, say this the wrong way, but I I don't feel like I have any pressure, honestly. Um, you know, I feel really great. I feel really excited. You know, instead of, you know, it being negative, it's really positive. I'm very excited about where we're headed. Um, but no, I don't feel any pressure. >> Obviously, last year didn't probably didn't go the way that you wanted it to with the Raiders, too. Do you feel like you still you have something to prove after a year like that? Yeah, I mean there's always going to be something to prove whether you win a Super Bowl, you make a Pro Bowl, if you're all pro, you know, it's a year-to-year league and so prove and that's internal. Um, I don't have anything to prove to anyone outside. You know, it's really about proving to myself and the guys inside this locker room that we can be the team that we, you know, uh, want to be. And, uh, we have a vision for ourselves, but all the outside noise, I, you know, I've developed, I don't know, a way to block it out. And, uh, you know, for me, I put the pressure on myself, though. you know, there is pressure within myself to get better every single day. >> What's been your impression of of Kade since you've got a chance to get him? >> Shoot, man. K's been doing great. Um, he can spin the heck out of the ball. Uh, I feel like he's a guy who's always prepared. He's been preparing um as if he's going to be a starter and that's something that's important in this league. You have to prepare every single day like you're the starter, like you're going to be out there playing. That's the only way to do it. And I and I've seen that from him. I think he's got a bright future. Gino, people always love a great comeback story. So with you, have you allowed yourself to think like how cool it would be if you were the guy, you know, to get this thing turned around here considering you were here so many years ago and come back and like >> Yeah. I mean, that'd be like a that'd be like a story in a movie, right? You know what I mean? It's kind of like one of those superhero movies. But, you know, my life is is based on reality and we got to focus on, like I said, getting better every single day. Um, you know, God has blessed me to play in the league this long and to have an opportunity to to come back here. Um, you know, I'm very very grateful for that. Uh, because they don't come too often. You know, these opportunities, you have to cherish them and and that's the way I look at it. I really cherish this opportunity. I really look forward to again just going to practice tomorrow and trying to get better. And uh, that's the way I'm going to treat this entire year and my the entirety of my the rest of my career. What would your What would your message be to Jet fans about you? >> Jet up. Let's go. >> What's up, man? Good to see y'all. >> What have you What have you learned about your new quarterback? >> Yeah, man. Uh he he's awesome to be around. He's uh really good communicator. Um able to digest this this stuff. We're all learning very well. Um and then not to mention, he just throws a really friendly ball. You know, one of those that that really easy to catch. you have no problem running right at it. It's um it's friendly. So, Gino's been been great these this last month and I I look forward to getting to know him even more. >> Gary, when you look back on last season, um just how difficult was that for you with the the injuries that? >> Yeah, it was um it was it was tough, man. It was one of those those things where, you know, in hindsight, I look at it and it's like, all right, maybe maybe you needed it. Cuz I hadn't been out with for, you know, extended period of time up to that point. And um it it really allowed me to change my point of view and just kind of look at some things from a different angle. So, you know, I don't want to sit here and act like I didn't get anything out of it, but but not playing football, you know, which is ultimately what I was brought here to do, it hurt me, you know, and it it it's uh it's never been brought upon me like that, you know. So, so it was a little different. But not to mention, I just Yeah, I just needed to change my my scope on things, right? That is what's at risk every time I take the field. And and you know, maybe I was getting a little bit too comfortable. So, um yeah, you know, I'm happy to be back now. How do you feel now? >> I feel great. I feel great, man. I didn't I didn't uh I surprised myself a little bit and you know, it took a little longer initially than I expected and, you know, we got to to the offseason and all a sudden I had time and and I was already ready to go a little bit sooner. So, you know, now it's just getting back comfortable playing, you know, getting getting back used to a guy on you while you're running route, stuff like that. Stuff you can't really mimic until you're doing the real thing. So, um I feel great. But as far as, you know, getting back to my to myself, I, you know, I got some work to do. I'm excited, though. I'm excited. It's It's going to be a journey. And, um, yeah, man. I'm not that far off. I don't want to scare nobody. I'm good. I just, you know what I'm saying? But, but, you know, I got a different standard that that I just want to get back to. And, and um, you know, that's the mission. >> When you say you maybe you got a little too comfortable, what do you mean by that? >> Um, just as far as, you know, going out to practice and not knowing what's at stake every time. we play a dangerous game, you know, and I think I think you know when you go I mean I had been since my senior year without missing time, you know, and that happened off the field. I never really had an injury happen on the field. And I and I think when when it goes like that, all of a sudden you start to get so used to playing that next Sunday coming that that practice, you going to have that opportunity to to correct that uh that route you didn't love from the game, right? But the reality of it is you got to have like a sniper mindset. you get one chance at this thing, right? And u that kind of brought it into perspective for me is what I meant by that. >> You talked about Priest obviously just signed his his new contract, what your reaction was when that happened and then you kind of mentioned this a little bit, but like have you guys like talked about how you look around and like a lot of the guys that you came in with and like it's been so much change over the course of these years. Yeah, >> no doubt. Um yeah, man. I I was just super excited to see Breeze get locked up cuz cuz that's one of the guys I came in with and you know that day we got drafted. Y'all probably some of y'all probably remember like, you know, we had big plans and you couldn't have told us we weren't going to go accomplish, you know, everything we had talked about as a group, you know, and uh to look around and still know that, you know, I got a guy that we talked about that I talked about that with um and that, you know, we didn't it's not a failure. It it got delayed. You know, it sucks to see some of the guys that we came in with not here as far as just just like what Bree is talking about. But that's the reality of this thing when you don't go play good ball. So, so the reality of it is we got to figure this thing out. And we are. We're on the we're on the proud to do it. And you got a guy like Bree to make it a whole lot easier, man. He's special at what he does. One of the best in the league. And and I'm excited that they uh that they locked him down cuz we going to need him, man. That boy can can play. And not to mention, he just knows what it what it's going to take to to turn this thing around and he's excited for it, you know. So, >> what have we learned about you? You know, the person like dealing with him and everything like that because he's obviously been through a lot. No, 100%, man. And you start to realize like you people go through a lot and how do they come out on the other side of that? And when I met him, it was like, oh, that's how he came out of it, man. He's a a top-notch human, you know, a guy that uh as a receiver, you know, we we we we search out for we want to talk to our quarterbacks. We want to have those conversations. We want to um know what they're thinking, you know, cuz at the end of the day, we we want to catch the ball, right? So, it's like, "Hey, what are you thinking so I can catch the ball?" And uh that's the reality of it. and he's super receptive on all that been super awesome. Not to mention just the way he he was able to like he was so good at um verbalizing the offense and what coach Reich had talked about him or talked to him about early on that I thought it was Gino's offense that he had kind of brought with him from from the past. But no, man, he's just that receptive, that willing to to learn, you know, and I think that says a lot about someone and you start to realize, oh, he's been in here 10 12 years in the league. Um, I don't know how long he was here, but when he, you know, a lot of guys when they their first place and it didn't go the way they wanted to, they don't ever make that rise back to the top. Um you know, he's the most dominant pass rusher in the draft. If they come in and they're grateful for the opportunity and don't have a sense of entitlement, that's a that's a big separator. Um, because they're going to be appreciative of every day and they're going to put the work in. And only time that hard work hurt only time that hard work beats talent is when hard uh when talent doesn't work hard. when hard when when you're talented and you work hard, it's it's harder to miss than it is to make it. >> Take a couple more >> with uh David uh on your Onyum who you played with with the Saints. What is he going to bring to the defense and how much can he help the run defense? >> Um I don't want to make a preposterous statement, but cuz I played with a lot of guys, but he's easily top five, one of the best run defenders I've ever played with. I mean, he makes a noticeable difference in the in the game. Um, in our time with the Saints, every year that he was on our roster, we were in the top five of the defense of in the league. Um, in almost every category you look at, you go back and check that that that track record just especially in at at our height. I mean, he was just a big force, you know, especially on short yardage downs and uh when teams trying to uh run downhill or try to run stretch. He's just a guy who can can play on the back side of a play and the front side of a play. Commands double teams. Um and he's and he's effective as a pass rusher and putting pressure up the middle. Um but as a guy that that that will continue to champion for a defense, you have to stop the run to be an effective defense. And you need guys who can do it from the front from on the back end. Um, and you know when they snap the ball, it's just me versus the man in front of me. And when you have that mentality, the technique, you know, you can find that, but that mindset and he's one of the ones that that just has it. >> Take one more. >> Good. >> All right. Appreciate y'all. God bless.

title: Bosa, McCaffrey, Greenlaw, McKivitz Talk Offseason, Start of OTAs | 49ers
text: What has this process been like for you going after already going through it uh you know earlier in your career? >> Um it's different every time. Um definitely a long road. So, um, yeah, uh, it's it's going really well and I plan on on being ready. >> What you just mentioned about everything you well everything you just mentioned and you mentioned the process of the mind getting back there. He's my best man at my wedding and like even he still talks about it like when you understand the standard of what this franchise was built on and what the standard is and that's a six Super Bowl. um and you don't win it and it's the goal every year obviously and you want to uphold that standard and everyone un you know knows that winning is the ultimate goal here and you have that buy in from veteran players and a and a front office and then a coaching staff as well and the whole goal is winning uh it's hard for guys to turn that away like when they do go away and it's not the same that's what makes this place special and you know why I never want to leave and I'm sure why Drake you know came back >> why did you gold helmet and whatever that is. Have you talked to stribbling to get more insight into what a gold helmet actually is? >> No, I think it just has to do with, you know, high character guy plays the right way, plays physical, a leader. I'm sure that's when it comes down to, you know, they're scouting in college and there's a certain amount that they give out. Um, I didn't know at the time and then obviously now I get to understand what it is and I think I've fit that role pretty well now. >> You mentioned the left guard battle. What do you see early impressions of our guys at that spot? >> I think Connor KBY's come a long way. I think uh you never know how your rookie season's going to go. Uh it can be really good or really bad and um you know, you learn a lot. You're kind of flying by the seat of your pants and you don't really have a whole lot of technique. You're just thrown in and it's it's a whirlwind. So to see him play a lot faster right now, obviously it's OTAAS. um you know, we're not hitting uh we'll obviously see in July, but to see him kind of come out of his rookie season and, you know, take a breath and then now come in a little more rejuvenated, understands the scheme a little more to see him come out and and play faster, it's it's good to see he's a great guy. And then obviously you're going to have Rob Jones, another explosive guy coming out of Miami. So, uh it's going to be a fun battle in in July for that spot. But I think I think we've got some guys who can fill in that role. >> Last one, Jen. I think it's hard for us outside the building to understand. You think that every franchise would want a winning culture and to want to win. So, how explain how this building I know you've only been here, but I know you've got guys in your room that have gone off to other organizations without throwing anyone under the bus. >> Explain to us how this organization does that. there's not a lot of fluff. I think you know having not been anywhere it's all hypothetical right so there could be you know a lot of just distractions in buildings whether that's money or ticket sales or I don't know I'm not an owner I don't know so the way I see it is that um and what I've heard from other you know players that come here is that there isn't a sole focus on winning and when it and you kind of know going into a season if it's going to be good or bad uh just based on your team who you have, you know, what it feels like in the building. Um, but guys are drawn to this place. Um, and it is that feeling of winning. It is that feeling of, um, you know, there's a sole goal in mind in this building. Um, and it starts from the top down. And obviously when you have leaders like we do, that that goal is reciprocated and, you know, that's why guys flock here. >> Thanks. Appreciate it. >> Thanks, guys.

text: What's up, guys? Go ahead. >> Bunch of explosive uh playmakers looking for more explosives in the in the past game. Um and we're working through a lot of that stuff right now where you learn how to do that. Uh there's certain things with rules and things with safety that we gota can't fully go by. I mean we last saw them really click last off season. They all got hurt. Um have you seen improvement in their game other than them just simply being healthy? >> Uh yeah, definitely. I mean Ricky we got to see um throughout the year battling his injuries. Um, uh, Jordan and Jake, we didn't get to see quite as much of. Um, they all came back healthy. I was really excited how Jordan and Jake came back, though. You could tell they came back. It wasn't just healthy. You could tell they've been putting work in, and coming in here in shape and stuff has allowed them to get a lot of farther ahead in these five weeks than just coming here to get shape. They've come here to to me to to play and work. >> How are Bosa, Mike, and Keon White coming along from >> They're coming along. They're all in their rehab with a number of other guys. Um, a couple of those guys will have a chance at training camp and we'll see it with Mike as it goes. >> As you go about incorporating Mike Evans into his offense, what kind of unique characteristics and traits does he bring that maybe you guys didn't have? >> Um, I mean, I mean, Mike's just Mike's a Hall of Fame receiver. U, so just, you know, his experience of the game, what he's done in this league, just the respect he's earned. Uh that's different than you know I haven't had many guys like that except for um Andre Johnson and Julio just you know with the career he's had so far and just what's unique about Mike is his get off how he can attack down the field and I've never been around a guy that who's that tall with that long of arms um the competitor he is. So I'm excited to have the person or offense and the talent. >> Some similarities from where is coming from versus the program he's coming into. Has he seen to be able to catch off as quickly or what have you seen? Um, I mean, we've only been out there two days, but you know, he's done all our drills for the two weeks we had him in phase two. It's been awesome in the meeting rooms, works his tail off, and it's been good to watch him in two practices, but that's what they're going through right now. We throw a ton of stuff at him. Um, they usually do good the first couple days, they usually melt the second week, and they usually come back in training camp a little bit better for it. >> What have you seen from Brock Curry after watching his film from last year and how he's approaching the season? I know it's early, but >> um, like he always does. I mean, Brock always comes in here not to mess around, not to be complacent in anything. He's um always expects us to be hard on him through the tape. He's one of the most fun guys to coach because he's never sensitive and he's very deliberate in everything he does out there. >> Have you decided or have you worked with the coaches you're going to be going up against in the preseason as far as joint >> Yeah, most likely going to go up against Tennessee and the Chargers. And with the Chargers, is there any at all thought about, you know, you know, you're going to be playing them during the season as well? >> Like, does that factor into >> No, it's say pretty vanilla. You know, you're not scheming and stuff and doing stuff in practice, you know, it's just more getting guys a chance to go against a couple different things than they usually go against. >> Didn't see I know Evans was there yesterday. Didn't see him today. Is he around? Is you're just going to kind of spot some of these veterans and some of these work? Um, I mean, it's it's voluntary, so when they got stuff going on, you know, Mike had some family stuff he had to deal with back in Texas, I believe. So, he was here the last two days, but had to take out today and expect him to get back here next week. >> How come um M Jones didn't throw? >> His shoulder was a little sore today. Um, he said he could have gone through it, but it was unnecessary and um gave a chance for other guys to get more reps. >> Do you notice any sort of boost for Fred just having Dre around? >> Um, maybe a little. I think there's a boost for everybody. I think everyone loves Dre around just the way he carries himself, how into football he is and it's really cool when I talk to the team to sit back there see those guys shoulderto-shoulder and I seen them like that their whole careers together and there was one year off and um it's pretty cool to get him back for everybody but yeah Fred's excited. >> You have a few new defensive linemen. Do you get a chance to look at them at all right now even though like it really isn't going until >> Yeah, I think that's the biggest challenge about now. I mean, we look at them a ton in their individual drills and stuff and that's what they've been working on for really five weeks and these last two practices. You know, we did yesterday without helmets today with helmets just so they don't run into each other with their teeth. Um, but just the whole deal is nothing's full speed. So, you're using your hands, things like that, which is more assignment based is trying to give the safeties, the running backs the right look at what they hole they go to, but no one's out there really competing or trying to make a play. So, it's more about their conditioning and give them a chance to try to be ahead when we get to camp. >> One of the talking points during the draft was that Kalon Black didn't have many catches at Indiana. What have you seen from him as far as route running and just how comfortable he looks catching passes? >> I see a guy that I think could be developed in the past game. I mean, we definitely were excited about him for and the first thing we loved about him was him as a runner. Um, but we've we've gotten a lot of guys here who didn't start out great in the past game. Um, have the skill set to do it. They just haven't worked at it that much. And uh I know JP was like that. I know Elijah was like that. I thought those guys got a lot better. And I see Kaylin being the same way. He's got the skills to do it. Just needs to work at it. >> You ask the veterans to come in and really take charge and leaders throughout this whole voluntary workout. Do you have most of the guys here as Trent Williamson? >> Yeah, Trent Trent's the only guy who hasn't been here yet. He's coming here next week. Um everyone else has been good. Um you guys know Mike's missing today, but the everyone's been awesome. I mean, it's uh it's a little different than last year. I mean, last year we had such a mass exodus of people had been around and carried that team for about five years in a row that there was only about 12 13 specific guys I was kind of talking to. And now when I kind of talk to the leaders and kind of the makeup of our team, especially from last year and stuff, there's there's guys all over. I mean, it's a bigger group now. It isn't just veterans. There's some number of second year players have started two years. There's a number of third year players who are um and going into their fourth year have already started three years. So, a little different situation than last year with just the the group and overall different team that it's a different team than three years ago definitely, but it's um similar to the team we had last year. >> Conversations with KD about how he's feeling. I know he's out there a bit later. Is he saying anything interesting? I know some think he may come back early, but >> um I mean he's on track and very positive and happy every day um like KD is and doing good. I mean, KD works his tail off and he's extremely talented and gifted, so um he'll do it as fast as you can. >> Talked about how you had some of the veterans over to your house for dinner. What was your message to them? >> Um I mean I did that last year for the first time and I think I've told you guys about that or other people have. That was it was 13 guys and that was more it was all guys who had been here four years or longer. Um just to tell them kind of the difference going into this offseason compared to the previous five. I tried to do the same thing, but when I looked up there and tried to pick those guys, like there was too many of them now. There was too many guys who had kind of been a part of it. So, I just inviting guys, most of the starters who had been here the last two years. Um, it's tough. I can't invite 90 guys over to my house and I don't want to invite 50 guys over to my house right now. So, I got to have a spot to cut it off. Um, so it doesn't get too much. But um we just talked about how I wanted the guys to be in this off seasonason and just the group there that was starting and um doesn't mean they're guaranteed to start this year, but we're the group that kind of went through it together last year and just leading us this way. >> What other first impression of Osigi Zoo over the last few days? >> Um I mean, I've been extremely impressed with him since the day he got here. I mean, he um I've heard about it. It was advertised one. I always knew about him just from tape um once we traded for him, all the phone calls we got and the type of guy he is. But I he's been one of the best leaders on the team so far. Just how he works, how thorough thorough he is on everything, what he does on his own. Um, bringing guys along with him. Um, everyone from Dallas told us this and um, it's been that way. He's been a stud. >> Kyle, when you talk about that roster transition from two years ago to last year, you guys had set a high standard here and sometimes some get lost in translation in that type of transition. Do you feel like that standard has been either restored, maintained, kept intact or maybe even gone higher since that since that? >> Um, I mean I think we have a standard to we try to talk about a standard and how we work and how we approach each day which is with everything we got. Um, I think our standard for our team always tries to stay that way. I mean, I like to look at a standard for results and stuff, but I think that was more our message last year like we can't get obsessed with the results. uh you you tend to get obsessed with them especially with how close we've been. Um but I don't think that's the healthiest thing for our team. I didn't think it was last year. I think I kind of got my point across on that and um we had some success. Didn't get it never didn't accomplish the the one goal we're always setting out to do. Um but we had some success and now it starts over. >> Is Green Law definitely written in as as the weak side linebacker? I mean he has had some injury stuff but you just that that's the guy who's going to be at weak side. >> Yeah. Yeah definitely. Did you think about keeping D just to make sure or you were just >> Oh, we did. I mean, it's and lots of linebackers play also, you know. I mean, when it's base, there's three out there, so we would have loved to keep D. Um, we also just looked at our overall roster. When you look one to two years out, also knowing the number of unrestricted free agents we have, um, the number of guys that we do feel can make this team at linebacker. Um, the thought that we were going to add linebackers in the draft. Um, and then just it's hard to stockpile players. Um, and when you can add a draft pick and add a younger guy when you might be losing someone the next year and stuff. I mean, I last thing I wanted to do was trade D at all. We love D as a player. We love him as a person. Um, we know how much she'd help us as one of our top three backs. We backers. We know how much she'd help us if Dre or Fred got hurt. Um, but then you also look into contracts, how a year out and stuff that is, and what you're doing in the draft. And sometimes you got to make tough decisions like that that can possibly help you in the future. >> Be the leader at the strong side right now. Um, uh, there isn't a leader. It's open for everyone. I mean, GIF held that the strongest last year. Um, but it's open for everyone right now. >> The thoon at all be an option there or do you just want to save him to back up in the mic? >> Um, linebacker just like receiver and just like interior lineman. You got to be an option at all three. I mean, he only you only got so many people up on game day. So, you always got to be an option. U, we do believe Mike Tatum's strength. That's what he did in college. That's what we feel a skill set that's at the be best. But, um, we usually have five guys make it, sometimes six. Uh, you're always going to usually keep the best five or the best six, however that pans out. >> Did you say that that Nick Bos is here rehabbing? >> Uh, yes. >> And then what are the uh what's the interest level in signing his big brother? >> Um, I mean, I love signing good players. Um, but I mean my kids do Instagram and look at your guys stuff, so they ask me that all the time, too. Um, I'm not hearing about all that stuff much. I know I look at our team as kind of we have our team and anyone else that we can figure out to bring especially someone like that that would be awesome but um that stuff's not always possible. >> Been pretty vocal about >> going going to Australia week one but the league scheduled you guys three home games after that. Just your thoughts on that after going to Australia. >> Um I mean three home games is irrelevant. That doesn't mean anything. Um it means you're going to have three more road games in December and January. Um, so that's my answer on three home games. >> Where does Nick Martin stand in that linebacker room? He took a while for him to get on the field last year and once he did had that concussion that sort of >> Um, I think we got two guys who established as starters and I think we got a big time competition for three, four, five, and six. >> You were very positive about Jordan James at the end of last year saying that you were kind of keen to get him in but the opportunity didn't show up. What have you seen from him now back on the field? Um, similar to I think what someone asked earlier about uh Jordan Watkins and Jake, you know, I'm always curious how these guys are going to come back um when we see him for the first time in April um or the end of March, whenever that is. And um sometimes guys come off their rookie year and um they finally relax because they've been going since their bowl game since the combine and they come really out of shape and those are the guys that usually have a sophomore slump or um the guys that don't get it. And so I was really curious to see how he came back and it was really cool. He came back in shape on day one. U which I think has allowed him to really gain ground in these five weeks. Uh he didn't come here for us to get him in shape. He came in shape and it allows him to get better at football. >> What's going on with Gindo? >> Gindo towards Peek Lifton uh about a month ago. >> Is that a season ender? >> It's not a season ender. Um but it's right around the end of training camp. Um, as far as that strongside spot, uh, at linebacker, is it too much to to think that Jaden Duggar could come in and, you know, play that role? He seems kind of customuilt for it, but he's also a rookie. >> Yeah, I don't think it's too much. I mean, um, you know, we had we've had rookies come in here and play a linebacker. If you look at Green Law and you look at Fred, um, not trying to compare anyone to those two guys. Um, but it's always a possibility. I mean, the the spot is open. Uh we have two established guys and we can have an onthe- ball linebacker as a third, we can have an offthe-ball linebacker. Uh we got a number of different skill sets in that room this year and uh I think it'll be one of the more fun positions to watch how it plays out. >> Just reading between the lines, it doesn't seem like you're too thrilled about your schedule. Is that >> um I mean I try to answer questions without um like I told you guys when you guys asked I said when you get it you just deal with it and that's what I'm dealing with. Um, now you'd rather not travel that much, but you don't I don't care as much about that. It's more about recovery. >> Are you guys doing anything special with the Australia trip? Like what what's your how early you going to get in? Do you spend another night there? What what are you guys doing? >> Um, I mean, usually when you travel 19 hour flight, you know, you don't want to get there the day before. Um, because you lose like a whole day there, too, and you're just messed up. um the people we've talked to, you don't feel normal to like the third or fourth day. Um so we're going to probably we'd like to go out seven days early. Um but since it takes a day and a half to travel there, we're going to go nine. I think we leave on Wednesday and land on a Friday. Um so then we get there about seven days before a game. I think it's Friday. We play Thursday or Friday morning Australian time Thursday here. Um so that's it. >> The camp here a little bit, right? Because of that. Um, you have to. I mean, when we're we're starting, you know, everyone gets that by week after your fourth week, the whole NFL gets three bonus practices and four mandatory days off. Um, we're traveling on that third day to Australia. So, you kind of miss that that week to recover or and to have those days off and those bonus days. So, um, it ends up being about a week different than usual. >> You like have your extra week of practice here or in your mind you were having an extra week of practice there? Um, I would love to have three extra bonuses practice here and then four days off um like everyone, but when you open on a Thursday um on the other side of the of the world, uh you lose that because it takes a couple days to travel there. It takes a couple days to adjust >> earlier. The camp, >> we can't start camp earlier. Camp's based off of I think 15 days away from your first preseason game. So, you just lose those days. >> Have you already finalized plans for Mexico City? Will you do uh >> we haven't finalized it yet, but um I mean we'd love to stay here and go there. It's a shorter flight, but that's not really the issue. You know, the the main thing with Mexico City is it's um 2,000 miles higher than um Denver and so we like to get adjusted to that altitude. So, we'll probably go to Colorado Springs again like we did last time to get ready for that altitude and then probably go to Mexico City the night before. Do >> that straight from Dallas? We haven't decided that yet, but most likely we'll probably end up the Mexico City trip will probably be a longer one than Australia one just because of that. >> Good. >> All right, guys. Good seeing you guys.
