So yeah, I mean I wouldn't say it's a different perspective but you know I mean it is because you know after you go to another organization uh you just kind of realize you know all the things that you missed you know and you miss with the guys here and uh just the everyday stuff you know u after practice talking to them uh the guys on the team uh just being in the locker room with the guys on the team. So, uh, yeah, I mean, it was a it's a different perspective as far as like, you know, you you're a lot more thankful for, uh, you know, what you had and, uh, and yeah, I'm sorry, what was your rest of your question? >> I guess what I'm asking is, does it feel like you're there is more of an emphasis now that you're back in the building to do things? I know you were an energy guy when you were here. Is there more of an emphasis to be even more of that, even more vocal, even more knowledgeable for the younger rookies here? Is there a difference or are you coming back kind of the same as the way you were here before? >> Yeah, I mean you never you're never the same, but I mean I don't I ain't got to do nothing more than what I normally do and that's just play football. I mean I've never been a talkative guy, a loud guy that's doing all this and that's Fred's job. I mean I just repeat whatever he say. So uh yeah, that's never really been my role. My role, you know, was to go out there and and just have fun and play football. And I think that kind of just take care of itself naturally. you know, whatever passion and whatever, you know, all that comes from just, you know, just being myself and playing the game. So, it's not nothing more that I got to do or, you know, all I got to do is get the call, play ball. >> There's a high standard here. Did you kind of recognize that a little bit more% >> is is different here for sure. >> struggled to rush the passer last year. >> I know your former team last year, the Broncos, set the NFL record for uh sacks. Is there anything maybe while off the field you learned just as the defense as a whole like getting more sacks, interceptions, takeaways? >> Uh, I mean, I just learned that it's just, you know, some defenses work better for these people and some defenses work better for these people and, you know, that defense is set up for a great Dline to go and dominate. And yeah, so I mean it's I didn't learn no pass rusher moves, but yeah, I mean just seeing the difference between the defenses and how they operate, how this defense and a four down operate versus five down. Uh it's a lot of differences. Uh but you know, you got to have Dline for for both of those schemes to to get what you want done. >> What did what did you learn about yourself last year? >> That's a good question. uh a little bit of what I've already known, but uh you know when times get tough uh you know I can't you know ain't nobody ever to point the finger at and I don't blame nobody for the choices I make and for you know the way things happen throughout the year. uh never been that person to blame anybody, but um it's kind of more of what I've already known, but uh just uh honestly just like just resilience is as crap. like I mean it's just just I don't want to go into the season but um you know just it didn't go the way I wanted to but I know you know got the chance to play the last game versus the Patriots and uh no matter how the season was going you know I always just showed up ready to go ready to play and give it my all and uh and yeah so I mean something I've already kind of known but you know at the end of the day you know I've always been in a environment where I got my guys around me So, um, you know, to be in an environment where I ain't got nobody there, same as kind of how life has been, you know, and just continue to push and push and push and know that God going to put me in a position where I need to be and uh, he ain't going to set me somewhere supposed to be and I believe that full heartily. So, that's why I don't take nothing back and uh, yeah, I mean, something I've already known, but like yeah, God is definitely he got my back. So, >> standard, going back to that standard. Um there's been some personnel changes here uh since since you left. Um do you feel like that standard is still intact and do you feel like that window is still open for it to be as high as it has been in the past? >> Yeah, thousand%. I mean I mean even when I was gone I knew that San Fran was still going to have the capability of getting to the playoffs, getting to the Super Bowl, whatever is in store for him. And that's just because of the guys that's on the team. I mean, you got the best leadership, just just great quality of guys here. You know, you don't get that too many uh too many places. And um no matter what position it is, it's it's a leader somewhere and somebody that's, you know, you can look up to and say, "Okay, he's going to do his job." You know what I mean? So, um I think everything that's in store that we wanted, you know, five years down the road or five years before, we still got that same opportunity now. Like, I don't see no different. Um, if anything, I see more of a, you know, opportunity for us to do it just because like we're, I mean, we're veterans. We're we're vets. We didn't seen everything. And, uh, yeah, I mean, it's just our turn to get it done. So, >> you play the same speed. It seemed like your whole career, whether Arkansas, Denver, here. Um, it means a lot to you obviously. Where did that come from? Why does it mean so much to you? Uh, I mean, yeah, just, you know, growing up just like I said, just if you if I ain't got if I don't find a way to do it, then I nobody it ain't going to get done. You know what I mean? And, uh, yeah, I don't want to be the reason for it not getting done either. You know what I mean? So, um, you know, I've been through too much and come this far to get on that field and not give it everything I got. You know, there's there nothing's promised, nothing's guaranteed. I understand that, you know, I can tweak my ankle or this or that and who knows. So, um I don't know until like it's it's about every chance and every every time I get to get on that field like whether it's practice or whatever, just enjoying the moment and and just playing hard as hell because you don't know when your next opportunity is going to be. >> Last one. Branch, go ahead. >> Uh Dre, a lot of guys with Achilles say, you know, they can come back in nine months or a year, but they actually don't feel like they're back to like really back until I don't know sometime after that. I don't know if that was your experience, but um kind of when did you feel like okay, I don't have to worry about the Achilles anymore. I don't feel this. >> I kind of felt like that uh throughout the Denver season. That's when I kind of felt like all right like I kind of got adjusted to the normal and then uh you know uh still felt like you know was still kind of feeling it out you know uh but I felt like I got adjusted to the normal and then probably about midway to you know kind of once I got back and re uh from rehabbing with the quad a little bit uh I kind of felt like you know like I like I I could go and practice and I warm up and I could do and I don't got to worry about no pain, you know, nothing. So, I ain't got to worry about what shoes I got on, all that kind of stuff. So, I say probably about last year is when I first felt like, you know, for at least a week or two or multiple days in a row straight that I felt like, all right, I'm good to go now. So, and I've been feeling great in Achilles ever since. So, >> thanks, guys. Yep. Appreciate you. a lot of you guys today, huh? >> What are your impressions of the two uh offensive line draft picks? Uh both guys to have pretty good personalities. Did you have you picked up on that? >> Yeah, I think they're good rookies. Um, you never know how they are going to be until they get in the room and, you know, you see the draft process and how it works. Um, and then both Carver and Enrique are, you know, they fit well into our room. I think we're, you know, a lot better than what we have been before. So, to add these two guys and obviously you see that there's some explosiveness with both of them and, uh, they're both going to be good fits for the room. So, uh, excited to see what what they can do. And obviously, it's just OTAAS. So, you know, they're getting their first taste, but, you know, we'll see in camp. >> Stood out in the pre-draft process for his, you know, his speed and his athleticism. Is that something that's that's evident when you when you're out there at practice? >> Oh, yeah. Yeah. You can you can see it. Um, I mean that's obviously he's a little raw. So, um, you know, when it comes to the football side of it, you know, he's still going to learn and do that, but when it comes to a skill set and what a guy has available and tangible asset as a lang speed, you know, quickness, all that stuff, yeah, you're not going to find a guy who has more. >> Last year, you got a lot of questions about the the offseason exodus of all the guys leaving, what you guys were kind of uncertainty going into this year. This offseason, you guys reinvest in veterans and and guys who can help you win. just as an invested observer, what was it like this offseason kind of getting back to like adding and and going for it again? >> Yeah, it feels good. I mean, every year we all know the goal is Super Bowl and uh when you can add guys like, you know, Mike and Kirk and, you know, guys with real speed and and can get open obviously from a skill point. Um and then some of the guys we've added in our room as well. So, like when you when you got guys who are coming in and you see the front office working, putting in, you know, putting guys in early just even before the draft, it adds a little confidence that, you know, obviously they know there's a bigger goal at hand, but then, you know, you're seeing it back up for us, too. But, you know, our goal is always the same. >> Coming off of the year that that you had to did you feel like that, you know, you were maybe a little ahead of the curve in the reset that that what you guys did on the field maybe upped the urgency to get back to that what the office did? >> Yeah, I don't think, you know, there was a lot of hope for us last year. Uh that's for sure. But you know, I think we we rehashed everything, reset our goals as a team, what our rules were, who we were as a team, and then bringing along the young guys bought in, which was huge. You know, like there's a lot of confidence at the beginning of the season, but you saw guys like AC, um Stout, like a lot of these guys came in, Mike, um that came in and just played really well and bought in that, you know, there's a standard here at the Niners and and they played up to that. So, you know, you want to forget about the 24 season, but it was needed to to get the next to last year. So, um to have those guys come in and buy in. Now, it's, you know, their turn to talk to the rookies now and also our job as well as leaders of the team to be like, "Hey, this is the standard we've set and our goals playoffs every year in Super Bowl." But, you know, that wasn't even the calling card last year. It was just, you know, see where we are as a team and and go from there. So, yeah, we were playing with, you know, house money, but also like, you know, that's the goal in the the long run. I know last offseason you added the Vallejo Hill in your training regimen. Are you climbing a mountain this offseason or anything different that you're adding? >> Mountains of Idaho. Yeah, a little more elevation there, but uh no, I mean I love training in the city, you know, right off Front Street, Vallejo, Karnney, all of it, going up to Koi Tower, running the the brick staircases over there. So, uh it's cool to train and have a a little more, you know, city city behind you feeling at least uh in my training. >> Cool. There's five new guys in the room, three uh free agents, you got a couple draft picks. Is you is this the most Is this the deepest offensive line room that you've been in since you've been in the league? >> Yeah, I think I think it's one of them. I mean, 2021 we were pretty deep. We had a lot of older vets in that room. Um but I think this is from a overall standpoint for sure. Uh I think you know a couple of us said we we're better off at the beginning of this year than we have been I think since I've been here. Um so I think depthwise, yeah, we have it. We have the skill guys in there as well for us. So, uh, you got guys who can run and that's what this offensive line needs is guys who can run and get on guys and sustain blocks. >> And the fact that, you know, four of the five starters return, what does that continuity do for that unit to take that next step? >> I mean, it's everything when you can have guys who are playing together through big games like last year, um, year before that. I mean, Jake and Trent and I have played, you know, I think three years in a row now, going on four. Um, obviously Trent and Jake have played even longer together. And then now with Dom and I being, you know, going into what, year three, playing next to each other. So, just having that continuity and knowing what we're going to do when it comes to games or twists or just whatever comes up in a game, we can we're pretty adaptable and we we know how to work well with each other. And then having a guy who can come in as the, you know, the left guard, obviously the spots, everyone watching. So, um, if you can get a guy that can come in and fit into that role pretty well, then that's going to be, uh, even better for our group. But, you know, we're looking to be a top 10 unit like we have in the past, top 15, whatever that is. Um, but, you know, we've got a good group up front. When >> you go through a year like you guys went through last year, the transition that you were talking about, and then the injuries that you dealt with, and you still win 12 games and a playoff game, um, what does it say about that group last year, but also the future for what you guys are trying to do moving forward? >> Uh, it says that this group's ready to win. That's what it does. Um, you know, we didn't know last year what this team was going to do. There wasn't a whole lot of, you know, playoff talks, Super Bowl talks, whatever it was. It was just are you going to get better each week and win each week. So, um, when that eventually we got, that was the reward for that 12 win season. Um, yeah, it feels great. I think we're ahead of the curve, whatever that means, in a in a rebuild or however you want to call it, uh, doesn't really matter. There's two teams in our division. Obviously, Arizona is still going to be tough, but there's two who are at the top as well that ride along with us. So, um, are we ahead of it? I don't know. We'll see, you know, when we play in Melbourne, Australia, but, um, it's it's a good feeling going into into the next 40 days after this next week. So, um, you know, I think we're at a good starting point for this team. >> Um, you obviously, I assume, can afford groceries and everything after your contract extension, so you're doing okay on that front, >> but will you see like offensive linemen and how they get paid when they do reach free agency? Obviously, you know, you didn't know how the season was going to play out before you signed out last year, but was there any sort of like, oh man, it would have been nice to hit the open market or I mean, any any like regrets? >> No, not one. Uh, I mean, my goal never was to be the highest paid. That wasn't my goal. I mean, obviously money, it's you're in the NFL, like money is the main thing. Like, we all want to get paid. We want to have generational wealth. I want to have my grandkids have money, too. But uh with the contract I was offered and honestly I don't want to leave here. Like obviously being cut, I got some scars there. But like to be able to be cut, be a draft pick here, gold helmet guy, whatever that means. But like there was a reason why I was here, drafted here while I was cut here, why I still played here, and then now I've had um you know, three good seasons of starting and then going into the fourth. So like why would I you know the grass isn't always greener on the other side. I saw a lot of guys not get paid in free agency this year. So, there's a demand, whatever. But, you know, I like it here. I want to be on that 10-year wall. So, like there's there's a lot more besides the money uh that a contract gives you that's available in this town, in this city, that's more important to me than a dollar amount. So, the connections I make off the field in San Francisco and and what I'm doing, my you stuff in the city and in Idaho as well, there's no reason for me to to risk or just taking a chance to go somewhere else. >> Have you talked to about on that question. Drake Greenline kind of said the same thing. You know, going away from here, it's just different being away and then being able to come back. You're just more grateful to be here in this building, in this room with this team. >> If you could go into detail, what are those things? What is the difference from being away from here to then being >> I think there's a sense of family. Um, when you come here, like a lot of guys that do like Dre, there's a reason why he was drawn back here. Like when you have a core group of players who understand a winning culture, uh I talk to Charlie Warner all the time too. He's my best man at my wedding and like even he still talks about it like when you understand the standard of what this franchise was built on and what the standard is and that's a six Super Bowl. um and you don't win it and it's the goal every year obviously and you want to uphold that standard and everyone un you know knows that winning is the ultimate goal here and you have that buy in from veteran players and a and a front office and then a coaching staff as well and the whole goal is winning. Uh it's hard for guys to turn that away like when they do go away and it's not the same that's what makes this place special and you know why I never want to leave and I'm sure why Drake you know came back. gold helmet and whatever that is. Have you talked to stribbling to get more insight into what a gold helmet actually is? >> No, I think it just has to do with, you know, high character guy plays the right way, plays physical, a leader. I'm sure that's when it comes down to, you know, they're scouting in college and there's a certain amount that they give out. Um, I didn't know at the time and then obviously now I get to understand what it is and I think I've fit that role pretty well now. You mentioned the left guard battle. What do you see early impressions of the guys at that spot? >> I think Connor K's come a long way. I think uh you never know how your rookie season's going to go. Uh it can be really good or really bad and um you know, you learn a lot. You're kind of flying by the seat of your pants and you don't really have a whole lot of technique. You're just thrown in and it's it's a whirlwind. So to see him play a lot faster right now. Obviously it's OTAAS's um you know we're not hitting uh we'll obviously see in July, but to see him kind of come out of his rookie season and you know take a breath and then now come in a little more rejuvenated, understands the scheme a little more. To see him come out and and play faster, it's it's good to see. He's a great guy. And then obviously you're gonna have Rob Jones, another explosive guy coming out of Miami. So uh it's going to be a fun battle in in July for that spot. But I think I think we've got some guys who can fill in that role. >> Last one, Jen. >> I think it's hard for us outside the building to understand. You think that every franchise would want a winning culture and to want to win. So, how explain how this building I know you've only been here, but I know you've got guys in your room that have gone off to other organizations without throwing anyone under the bus. Explain to us how this organization does that. Um, there's not a lot of fluff. I think, you know, having not been anywhere, it's all hypothetical, right? So, there could be, you know, a lot of just distractions in buildings, whether that's money or ticket sales or I don't know. I'm not an owner. I don't know. So, the way I see it is that, um, and what I've heard from other, you know, players that come here is that there isn't a sole focus on winning. and when it and you kind of know going into a season if it's going to be good or bad uh just based on your team, who you have, you know, what it feels like in the building. Um but guys are drawn to this place. Um and it is that feeling of winning. It is that feeling of um you know, there's a sole goal in mind in this building. Um and it starts from the top down and obviously when you have leaders like we do that that goal is reciprocated and you know that's why guys flock here. >> All right. Thanks. Appreciate it. >> Thanks guys. That's it for today, guys.

title: Germie Bernard, Gennings Dunker, Riley Nowakowski Media Availability (May 28) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: A lot of run after catch was their was their asset. They love Deebo. Uh Tell me about that part of your game. Is it your strength? >> Yeah, I I believe so. I mean, you know, football is all about being selfless. So, it's it's always been in my repertoire. >> Pop Warner Pop Warner Pee Wee football, were you the kid scoring five six touchdowns? >> Yeah. Uh these guys are a lot faster than college linebackers. Um they're uh they're pretty quick, so you know, maybe taking a little bit different angles cuz they're definitely a lot better athletes than me. So, yeah. >> What have your impressions been of uh Jerry Allen so far this year? >> I mean good. He's done a really good job and he's been a great leader and he's having a good time, too, so you know, he's a good guy. >> Toryn, that's a unique first name. How did you get What What's behind that? >> my mom just came up with it, honestly. I think >> Doing what you guys did individually and collectively? >> Yeah, for sure. I think number one just playing a longer season helped out a lot, you know, I mean we play a 17-game season nowadays in this league. So, you know, it's a little bit a little bit longer. So, I felt like I got a little intro into that last year and then, you know, just how to prepare and and how to approach the season. I think I took a big step in that last year and kind of started approaching it in a more professional way. So, I think that helped a lot. >> got to Wisconsin, Indiana was still Siberia. >> All right. How'd you do it? >> Uh shoot, that's that's a question for Sig, you know what I mean? Like we had we had a great group of guys, you know, and it was really just a lot of team work. >> well, now you went after the good season. >> But, I mean, when you went to Wisconsin you probably never thought, "Boy, Indiana's going to win the title in 2020." >> No, definitely not. You know, I mean, watching the Big Ten my whole life, you know, you don't really, you know, expect a whole lot of Indiana a lot out of Indiana in football. But, you know, they they really changed that narrative and it's a powerhouse program now. So, I I was happy to be a part of it. >> But, does that take some intangible or some some character? Do you feel like >> Mhm. >> you got a little something in the tank >> Yeah, for sure. >> not have? >> Yeah, I think I think that's what what Sig does. He brings in guys that are really committed and and ready to work and I think that's what a difference that he has, you know, he he really vets people in the process and makes sure that they fit in with the team and they fit in with, you know, what what our culture's trying to be and how we're trying to get things done.

title: Coach Mike McCarthy Media Availability (May 28) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Uh yes, it's uh it's been a very very productive week. Um like you know always uh I look back at the history of of OTAAS uh like today is OTAA number five, you know, install number five. So you get to five, six, and seven. This is usually where the rookies kind of hit the wall a little bit and uh you didn't see that today. So I've been I've been really impressed with the way they've come in and you know picked it up and have lined and tried to learn from the the veteran players. So it's going well. you know, we're operating in the, you know, CBA tempo and everything, but I think the teaching and really the video that we've been able to to gather from these these OTAA practice has been excellent. So, um, you know, we're on we're on we're on pace to get all the work that I that I want to get done before we conclude and just been real impressed with impressed with the, you know, with the work ethic of our men. So, it's it's been a good week so far. Michael Ramon was saying yesterday that uh 55 touches and completions is a big number for you. How did you come about that number? Is there like a win loss percentage associated with that number? >> Well, I mean it's it used to be 53. I I just think as you know as offenses have prevailed and with the role changes over time, you know, I I I started off in you know 1993 working in game analysis and that was a big part of my job as a young coach. So we've always stayed in touch with the numbers. They call it analytics now. Uh but you know I think it's important to to use those guidelines to to project uh goals. Uh but it also it helps uh keep you on a path for mindset of how you want to how you want to call a game. Uh there's no absolutes. Uh but I think it there's more to the 55. It's a you know I've always believed in a complimentary football formula. You know that comes with great defense. you know, obviously getting those touches to your perimeter players. Uh the big one is obviously winning in the, you know, the turnover ratio and time of possession. So, those those are the things that, you know, when we get into the real football because right now we're in a teaching phase. Uh that's been really the emphasis for year one here to get everything taught schematically. Uh we've been, you know, going at the last two weeks on situational football, but we'll get heavier into those types of conversations. I don't know what the hell Tim's doing giving that good information out so early. I would have a talk with him. But um >> what kind of percentage you come up with on what do you mean? >> Win loss like if you get to 53 or 55. >> Oh, I mean it's high. I I but you know like like I said there's there's more to it. It's part of the you know complimentary football you know formula. I mean you could you could have you know 32 rushes and you know 25 completions but you turn the ball over and you know give give up point. So it's it you know it's part of that formula. you know, it's a it's an offensive focus and and the reality of it is it's it's playing the quarterback position the way we want to play and we want to, you know, big part of our job is getting the ball distributed. So that's where the play caller and quarterback, you know, we want to be connected. >> Mike, Rico said that when you got hired, his mother texted him and said, "You're going this way." And as soon obviously it sort of turned out like that a few months later. What makes him good a good at his job and why is he a good prince for what you try to do? >> Well, mothers know best. I mean, we we recognize that always. Um, but you know, Rico's, you know, Rico's a great foot fit for for how we're going to play here in Pittsburgh and and I' I've been blessed to just be part of his journey. I've, you know, watched him grow up as a young player in Dallas. You know, he went through a lot of adversity there early in his career, you know, with the injuries the first two years and I really had to wait probably longer than I know he would have liked to for his opportunity. And I just I've been just so impressed with him and uh just how diligent of a football player he is. I mean, he's really smart. You can see his background. You know, he's a quarterback, you know, in his high school days. So, uh he has a really high understanding of how the game's played, but you know, he's tough as nails. You know, I I love his running style and he's a great fit with Jaylen and he's a great fit for us. So, what you just said, do you see this as being even in light of all these receivers that you've added in Aaron Rogers power offense? >> Definitely. I mean, you got you got to be it's uh I mean, that's the way you draw it up and and you know, 17 games, it's a long year. Uh winter football is when it is most important. Winning in November, December, and January. Uh so, this team is built that way and that's the way we'll play. So, uh, but you have to be able to beat teams any way you need to. And I think that's the important, you know, the importance of, you know, building a diverse offense. Uh, but it'll always start with defense, running the football, special teams, and the ability to score, you know, whatever way we need to. So, uh, that's what we're building. That's why we're taking the time and really putting the energy into this, you know, scheme development, you know, scheme installation phase here. So, and I, like I said, I think our guys have done a nice job. But what's the role of a fullback in that traditionally? Do you always used one? Do you use one if you have one? >> Yeah, definitely. I I think systems, you know, if if you have a system that cannot utilize the, you know, the strength of the personnel that's available, then I think you have to you have to take a hard look at your system. And I've I've started my journey in coaching in the two back offense and and I and I still believe in the principles of it. Still teach from the the foundation of two back offense. So, um, you know, whether you're using that with a traditional fullback, um, because, you know, if you just look at it from the the business and, you know, development of a roster, you know, your fullback has to has to play special teams. You know, you can't have players that only have one job, you know, and so that's that's part of why I think sometimes fullbacks, you know, you don't see as many of them. Uh so um and we feel like we have you know we have some guys to work with here. But you know the fullback tight end position, the versatility and the position and and scheme and and skill set uh you know flexibility is important for those groups. But yeah, definitely I would always prefer to have a fullback. You know, I've played with as many as three fullbacks on a 53man roster in my time as a head coach. So I think it's an important position. I think it's it's part of, you know, playing Pittsburgh Steeler football and um and we'll definitely tilt that way. >> like like Roman Wilson, what what's going to be the key for him to take another step? >> Just keep doing exactly what he's doing. He he he's he's been here from day one. uh he was one of the first first men to to reach out you know just clearly ask you know what the expectation was of him how I viewed him um you know how I saw him fitting in as the rules you know the rule as far as X you know F and Z and uh and he's doing the work you know he he's had a great offseason so I just need him to keep showing up and keep working his tail off because he he's got a he's got a skill set there's a lot there to work with so Roman's done a really nice Mike, for the returning players, how do you feel that they are doing with adjusting to the way you work out? >> I I think our veterans have done a excellent job. You know, I'm I'm a big believer in consist consistent consistency and regularity and and you have to have that from your experienced, you know, players and your coaches. you know, it's uh you know, who wants to work with someone that's different every day because you know, and that's I think that starts at the top and uh because if that's the case, that's probably where you're going to play, you know, when the games come. So, I think our veteran players have come in and um and we've been very, you know, upfront and frank and direct with them and as far as how we see see them and the direction that we're going. Um, I think we did a really good job of identifying uh the things that that have that were that you know that were done at a high level here and try to maintain as much as that as we could throughout our scheme development. Um, so that's been an adjustment. You know, you know, I'm in the process. I just completed a, you know, 100 day report, you know, first 100 days on the job. So, and that's been filtered throughout our coaching staff. So, you know, there's there things that you can you can definitely learn in those first 100 days. I've learned through experience and it's more important for me to listen and observe right now than than talk. They you know, they're going to get tired of talking to me at some point, but it won't be during these these the you know, this first 120 days on the job because uh it's important for us to learn each other and there's just there's just a lot there's a lot to do in the first year. And I think you have, you know, for this being the third time going through it, you understand that, you know, everything we do has a progression and a regression to do it, whether it's the strength and conditioning, whether it's a training room, especially the coaches and scheme development, you know, fundamental development, game management, you know, installation, all that. So, you got to keep progressing, but you still have to have the feedback because if you have to regress, you take a step back and keep moving forward. So, um, and I I do I I really appreciate the way, uh, our men have, you know, consistency just, you know, come in here every day and work because that that's that's what we need to do. I mean, you know, the pompoms flying around and yelling, screaming, ain't going to do now. We need to learn the offense. Learn the defense. Make sure we know the special teams. Make sure we have a clear understanding of the fundamentals. Make sure each player has a toolbox that's full. Make sure they they have successful. Don't give them too much. You know, keep building that in a progressive regressive way. You know, all those things, game management, situational football, can't do enough of it. So, I mean, that's just really been our approach. It's been a very, you know, very hectic, busy offseason, but it should be. It's year one. I mean, this this is what year one looks like. And but at the end of the day, the players have responded. They're doing the work. I mean, I think you see it out here. I mean, this is a teaching environment. Um, you know, we we go to the CBA tempo like like you have to and but there's a lot there's there's a lot getting done here. You know, there's a lot more cameras here than you probably seen before and we're able to capture a lot of video and and and our guys are into it. So, uh, it gives us a chance to move the needle forward. >> You were talking with Joe Wick yesterday about his role in the defense.
